At the package level, we focus on thermal interface materials (TIMs) with emphasis on their structure-property relationships and thermal performance enhancement strategies. Across these different levels, a common principle emerges: intrinsic thermal conductivity alone is insufficient to determine the thermal performance of a material after integration, because dimensions, processing-induced changes, and interfaces are also important. By analyzing materials along the internal heat-dissipation pathway, this review identifies the key thermal bottlenecks and defines the material and interface requirements for a low-resistance internal heat-dissipation pathway in future electronic devices with high power density and a high degree of integration.

title: From Water Vapor Transmission Rate (WVTR) to Intrinsic Water Vapor Permeability (WVP).
abstract: NA: Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) is widely used to assess breathability in skin-interfaced electronics. In gravimetric wet-cup tests, however, the measured flux depends on transport through both the membrane and the apparatus. Apparatus resistance can dominate measurements of highly permeable membranes. Evaporation, headspace transport, membrane permeation, and external vapor spreading are modeled as resistances in series under a common chemical-potential driving force. The apparatus coefficients are calibrated using open-cup measurements in the same setup, independently of the reference permeability. For poly(dimethylsiloxane) membranes, where membrane resistance dominates, both a literature air-gap correction and the calibrated model reduce deviations from the reference. For a highly permeable anion-exchange membrane (AEM), the air-gap correction becomes unstable. Relative to a dynamic sweep-cell reference, the calibrated model reduces mean absolute relative deviation from 49.8% for classical conversion to 6.2%. It also provides model-based criteria for geometry selection and measurement duration, together with a procedure for converting WVTR to water vapor permeability (WVP).

title: Water-Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation.
abstract: NA: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron-to-submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood-based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood-based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m-2 h-1 in wood-based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water-heat management strategy provides a scalable, low-cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.

title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti-Ambipolar Characteristics in n-Type Organic Mixed-Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons.
abstract: NA: Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio-realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long-term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti-ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti-ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF-ON-OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti-ambipolar stability in non-ladder-type anti-ambipolar materials. Here, the n-type OMIEC, P(gNDI-gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti-ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion-permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling-induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low-power, fast-spiking Hodgkin-Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

title: Bottom-Cell Engineering as the Key to Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have emerged as a highly promising thin-film photovoltaic architecture, combining the exceptional efficiency potential of perovskites with the industrial maturity of CIGS technology. Despite rapid advances in perovskite top cells, overall tandem performance remains fundamentally constrained by the CIGS bottom cell, which critically governs bandgap matching, voltage losses, and interfacial recombination. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent progress in CIGS absorber and interface engineering for tandem applications. We highlight key strategies including Ga-gradient bandgap engineering, alkali post-deposition treatment, Ag alloying for low-temperature growth and bifacial operation, as well as buffer-layer and intermediate recombination layer optimization. We further discuss how surface morphology and defect chemistry collectively dictate carrier recombination dynamics and interfacial stability in monolithic device architectures. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward the commercialization of perovskite/CIGS tandem photovoltaics. By linking materials-level engineering with device-level constraints, this review establishes a unified framework to guide the development of high-efficiency, scalable, and industrially viable tandem solar technologies.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming.
abstract: NA: Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten-salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI-K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano-derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole-polaron absorption and extends the average exciton-associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap-assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI-K photoreforms alkaline-pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target-product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g-1 h-1, with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two-electron oxidation of surface-bound α-hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Waveguided, Self-Sensing Sheath-Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators.
abstract: NA: Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard-to-access environments, while providing integrated self-sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next-generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath-core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near-infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load-bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real-time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self-sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

title: Air-Stable Radical Additives Modulate Spin-Dependent Recombination in High-Efficiency Organic Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Triplet-associated recombination remains a potential loss channel in high-efficiency nonfullerene organic solar cells, particularly when separated charges re-encounter to form spin-correlated charge-transfer or polaron-pair states. Here, we introduce the air-stable organic radical TTM-1Cz as an additive to manipulate the triplet formation by the single electron-occupied doublet state characteristic of radicals. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurements confirm that the radical character of TTM-1Cz is retained after solution processing. Grazing-incidence wide-angle x-ray scattering measurements show that TTM-1Cz and its structurally related closed-shell analogue αHTTM-1Cz induce comparable, modest increases in crystalline coherence, indicating a structural contribution associated with the common molecular framework. In contrast, charge-separated-state-normalized transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a pronounced reduction in the late-time triplet-associated signal only in the TTM-1Cz-containing blend. Together with magneto-photocurrent measurements and local molecular-complex calculations, these observations are consistent with an additional, radical-specific perturbation of spin-dependent charge-transfer recombination. The optimized D18:L8-BO:TTM-1Cz device achieves a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.63%, with a certified efficiency of 20.45%. These results reveal a design principle for radical additives in organic solar cells, in which molecular-packing effects and spin-active modulation of recombination act as distinct but complementary contributions.

title: Dynamic Molecular Scaffold Enables Thermomechanical Stress Regulation and Adaptive Defect Healing for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Thermally induced stress accumulation is a major origin of lattice disorder, defect evolution, and ion migration in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), limiting their long-term operational stability. We develop a dynamic molecular scaffold strategy based on the adduct of α-lipoic acid and N-hydroxysuccinimide ester to mitigate thermomechanical degradation through simultaneous thermomechanical stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing. During film formation, DL-α-lipoic acid-N-hydroxysuccinimide ester (LA-NHS) undergoes in situ polymerization to establish a crosslinked polydisulfide scaffold at grain boundaries. The dynamic scaffold accommodates thermally induced lattice expansion and contraction, dissipates accumulated stress, anchors the perovskite lattice, and continuously passivates stress-generated defects through reversible disulfide-bond exchange, thereby preserving lattice ordering and improving the thermal durability. Consequently, the optimized PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.19%. The devices retain 91.71% of their initial efficiency after 150 thermal cycles between 15°C and 100°C, and 85.72% after 1500 h at 85°C. The strategy is successfully translated to large-area PSCs (25.02% for 1 cm2 and 22.06% for 10 × 10 cm2). This work establishes a dynamic molecularscaffold framework for managing thermomechanical degradation through stress buffering, lattice anchoring, and adaptive defect healing, providing a route toward efficient, durable, and scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Layered Precursor-Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In2O3 Approaching the Thickness Limit.
abstract: NA: Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor-guided synthesis of atom-thin amorphous indium oxide (In2O3) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In2O3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In2O3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance-voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 1018 cm-3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 1010∼1011 cm-2·eV-1. We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement-mode transistors with sub-3 nm channels, featuring near-zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate-stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high-performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next-generation nanoelectronics.

title: Maleimide-Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic-Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis.
abstract: NA: Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals. The regulation of biotic-abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide-functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI-gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio-interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis, resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23-fold increase in electron transfer and a 6-fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis. Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non-covalent group, yielding a 2-fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2-fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI-gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio-interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic-abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk-adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular-level interface engineering.

title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt-Free Ultrahigh-Ni Cathodes.
abstract: NA: Eliminating Co from ultrahigh-Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li+ transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics-guided defect-engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt-free ultrahigh-Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high-valence dopants reveals that Te6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi0.948Al0.045Te0.007O2 containing coherent local antisite-ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2-H3 phase separation and c-axis contraction, and preserve low-barrier Li+ migration pathways. Local Te-O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen-loss-induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g-1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability-transport trade-off in cobalt-free ultrahigh-Ni layered cathodes.

title: Multi-Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer.
abstract: NA: Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge-transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi-hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge-transfer energetics. Using a sulfur-rich amorphous CoReS2+x cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi-hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron-deficient interfacial state. This adsorption-driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first-principles calculations. The resulting a-CoReS2+x/CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass-derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi-adsorbate-induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy-conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.

title: Engineering Li+ Transport in Ni-Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization.
abstract: NA: Nickel-rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next-generation lithium-ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg-1, but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li+ transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li+ transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo-mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li+ transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport-centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross-scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport-centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next-generation high-energy-density cathode materials.

title: Kirigami-Inspired Stretchable Silicon Solar Cell Modules as Portable Power Sources.
abstract: NA: The integration of photovoltaic modules into wearable electronic devices represents a pivotal advancement for enhancing portability and sustainability. Despite their high efficiency and stability, traditional silicon solar modules are brittle, preventing their applications in mechanically flexible and impact-resistant wearable devices. Herein, we present a novel approach to deformable silicon solar cell modules of different sizes utilizing flexible kirigami-structured substrates integrating commercial silicon cells, enabling durability against continuous deformations caused by body movements. For instance, our Module-14-7S2P, consisting of 14 silicon solar cells, exhibits a power output of 37.50 mW while maintaining > 95% power retention of its original power output after 5000 deformation cycles and > 94% power retention after 120 h of water immersion. Furthermore, upon deformation to a 13% strain, this module retains ∼80% of the initial power output, data supported by FEA simulations. Our study provides new possibilities for employing silicon solar cells in wearable applications, accelerating the adoption of sustainable and portable wearable electronic devices powered by solar energy.

title: Near-Infrared Imaging of H2O2 in Plants With Nanosensors Under Environmentally Changing Conditions.
abstract: NA: Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion, and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H2O2. Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H2O2 sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ∼1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EB-NS, 900-955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (∼641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind-induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H2O2 monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single-channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress-induced H2O2 under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference-resistant optical sensing and advances field-deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.

title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid-Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next-generation high-energy-density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent-salt-additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high-voltage tolerance, fast-charging capability, and wide-temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid-phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new-type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt-solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high-concentration electrolytes, and developing brand-new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.

title: Supramolecular Stabilization of Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Durable Perovskite-Organic Tandem Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Perovskite-organic tandem solar cells (PO-TSCs) offer a compelling platform for flexible photovoltaics by combining wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells with mechanically compliant organic rear cells. However, their long-term stability is critically limited by the intrinsic instability of WBG mixed-halide perovskites. Here, through systematic ageing and mechanistic analyses, we identify halide phase segregation in the WBG perovskite sub-cell under photothermal stress as the dominant degradation pathway that dictates the operational stability of the PO-TSC investigated here. To address this challenge, we develop a halogenated cyclodextrin-based supramolecular strategy that enables precise regulation of perovskite crystallization, defect passivation and halide distribution. Synergistic host-guest, hydrogen-bonding, halogen-bonding and coordination interactions simultaneously regulate crystallization and suppress ion migration to result in stabilized halide homogeneity. Consequently, 1.80-eV WBG devices achieve 20.60% efficiency with improved operational stability. Integrated PO-TSCs deliver an efficiency of 27.17% (certified 26.3%) together with T80 lifetimes of 1100 h under maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and T85 lifetimes of 1128 h under thermal stress of 85°C, while flexible PO-TSCs reach an efficiency of 24.00%. This work defines a general supramolecular design paradigm for efficient, durable and flexible tandem photovoltaics.

title: Fundamental Inhibition of Polyiodide Formation by a Site-Separated Binder for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc-Iodine Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous Zn-I2 batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage systems, yet their practical performance is severely limited by the formation and shuttling of polyiodide intermediates. Here, we report a site separation strategy to block the generation paths of polyiodides and address the related issues from the source. This is realized with a site-separated polymer (SSP) binder that strongly and selectively confines I2 and I- at varied functional groups on different side chains. It disrupts their coupling to generate polyiodides chemically. Meanwhile, these effective interactions regulate the thermodynamic features of iodine species, which disfavors the formation of polyiodide intermediates and promotes direct I2/I- conversion during electrochemical reactions. The binder also reinforces cathode integrity at different iodine loadings. Therefore, the I2/SSP cathode delivers 212 mAh g-1 capacity at 0.2 A g-1 and retains 102 mAh g-1 at 50 A g-1, superior to 172 mAh g-1/11 mAh g-1 with the conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. I2/SSP also realizes 97.1% capacity retention over 31000 cycles at 20 A g-1, again far exceeding 46.8% after 20000 cycles for I2/PVDF. Under a high iodine loading of 50 mg cm-2, the I2/SSP cathode further achieves 10.1 mAh cm-2 capacity with 97.9% retention over 400 cycles.

title: "Activation-Resistance Elimination" Regulation by Lanthanide/Transition Metal Ion-Coordinated Nanostructures Intensifies Cuproptosis and Tumor Immunotherapy.
abstract: NA: The therapeutic efficacy of cuproptosis is constrained by its insufficient activation and resistance mechanisms. Here, a lanthanide/transition metal ion-coordinated nanoparticle, La-Cu@Lap/IWR-1, with optimized coordination, has been proven to achieve remarkable results in realizing comprehensive resistance-eliminating cuproptosis activation. La3+ not only enhances Cu2+-mediated multiple enzyme-mimetic activities via coordination to amplify oxidative stress but also disrupts lysosomal acidification to improve copper ion availability. Moreover, combined with lapatinib (Lap), it alleviates the shielding effect of mediator of cell motility 1 (MEMO1) on Cu2+, significantly strengthening the cuproptosis activation efficacy. Meanwhile, the released Wnt inhibitor IWR-1 can not only inhibit the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway that is concomitantly activated during cuproptosis induction to weaken the oxidative stress tolerance of tumor cells but also synergize with Lap to downregulate hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) expression, thereby effectively eliminating cuproptosis resistance. This comprehensive cuproptosis not only triggers significant immunogenic cell death but also synchronously inhibits key steps of tumor metastasis, such as epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix remodeling. This work proposes a therapeutic strategy for achieving comprehensive resistance-eliminating cuproptosis activation using lanthanide/transition metal ion coordination nanomaterials, providing a new entry point for tumor therapy.

title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair.
abstract: NA: Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre-programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow-degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell-instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non-degrading or fast-degrading hydrogels. Slow-degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long-term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: Nb5+-Induced-CeO2 Lattice Strain for Robust and Scalable Solar-Driven Ammonia Synthesis.
abstract: NA: Ammonia (NH3) underpins fertilizer production and is emerging as a renewable-energy carrier. Solar-driven gas-phase N2/H2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H2-rich conditions. Here, Nb5+ incorporation into CeO2 contracts the lattice and induces compressive microstrain, suppressing excessive oxygen-sublattice reduction and preserving Ru dispersion. In situ NAP-XPS and computational results show that Nb-CeO2 maintains an electron-enriched Ru working state under reaction conditions, which is further promoted by illumination. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO2 achieves an NH3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g-1 h-1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N2-activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NHx hydrogenation and NH3 desorption. Scale-up synthesis affords a 3 wt% Ru/Nb-CeO2-L catalyst stable for 480 h and operable under outdoor concentrated sunlight. A screening-level analysis estimates a catalyst-and-feedstock cost of 286-322 USD tNH3 -1 under the lower-bound electricity scenario, 42%-51% below the selected Cs-Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar-driven ammonia synthesis.

title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem-Cell-Based Tendon Repair.
abstract: NA: Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D-MRI with real-time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering-precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF-mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC-based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.

title: Ion-Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All-Solid-State Li-S Batteries.
abstract: NA: All-solid-state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active-material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li2S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface-bound ion-electron convergent interphases on the Li2S surface that reconstruct localized triple-phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li2FeS2 is identified to form a robust surface-bound interphase with Li2S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li2S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm-2 while delivering a loading-insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm-2, respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm-2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface-bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion-electron transfer (CIET) in all-solid-state batteries.

title: Life-Cycle-Sustainable Capacitive Deionization Enabled by Organic Molecular Engineering for Selective Ammonium Capture.
abstract: NA: Selective ammonium (NH4 +) recovery from complex wastewater streams remains a pivotal challenge in sustainable nitrogen management. Capacitive deionization (CDI) offers an energy-efficient electrochemical route for ion separation, yet its practical application is constrained by the inherent trade-off between NH4 + adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we circumvent this fundamental limitation through the rational molecular engineering of an organic electroactive material, 1,4-bis(1H-imidazo[4,5-b]phenazin-2-yl)benzene (IPB), which features extended electron delocalization and abundant C═N moieties for NH4 +-specific redox-coupled capture. The resulting IPB-based CDI prototype delivers a high NH4 + adsorption capacity of 267.23 mg g-1 and a fast rate of 62.51 mg g-1 min-1, while sustaining remarkable selectivity in complex multi-ion matrices, thereby effectively surpassing the conventional capacity-selectivity trade-off. Notably, CDI adsorption reduces wastewater NH4 + levels to below 3 mg L-1 and achieves 82.3% direct recovery as liquid fertilizer during CDI desorption, as demonstrated by isotope tracing experiments. The CDI process exhibits a low carbon footprint of only 4.66 × 10-2 t CO2-equivalent per tonne of NH4 + treated, underscoring its superior life-cycle sustainability. Therefore, this work proposes a molecularly engineered organic electrode material for high-performance wastewater remediation and circular nutrient recovery, paving the way toward carbon-neutral electrochemical water treatment technologies.

title: Entropy Stabilized Li-Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High-Voltage Cathodes.
abstract: NA: The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small-particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser-induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high-entropy doped Li-rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high-voltage performances. The direct bottom-up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li-rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic-resolution imaging, operando x-ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut-off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition-metal framework in the high-entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5-4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg-1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high-voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high-voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next-generation energy storage research.

title: Biointerface-Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria-Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity.
abstract: NA: Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune-beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface-customized nanomodulator (C/C-HP@M2M-TPP), developed through a biointerface-engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria-specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria-directed subcellular localization. Co-delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface-customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Ionic-Ligand-Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg-1 Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic-ligand-assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI- anions, creating anion-rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li+ hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm-1) and an exceptional Li+ transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li-metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid-state Li||LiNi0.9Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high-energy-density (515 Wh kg-1) solid-state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high-loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm-2) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic-ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high-performance and high-safety solid-state batteries.

title: Wafer-Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c-Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation.
abstract: NA: Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non-uniformity, and the need for post-growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2-inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp2-hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long-range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate-tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: In-Situ Self-Evolving µ-Sn10Bi Cross-Interlocked Structure and Three-in-One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low-Temperature Sodium Storage Performance.
abstract: NA: Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low-voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high-energy-density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long-term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three-in-one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ-Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ-Bi. Interestingly, µ-Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross-linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long-term structural stability of µ-Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in-situ formed further accelerate e-/Na+ transfer. As a result, the prepared µ-Sn10Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure-activity relationship of µ-Sn10Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low-cost, high-capacity, structurally stable, fast-charging anode with wide-temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Synthesis of Ti2B2Clx MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives.
abstract: NA: The unique properties and application possibilities of two-dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti2InB2 with ZnCl2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti2B2Clx MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 < x < 1.4. Further, in situ x-ray diffraction indicates a direct biphasic transformation from Ti2InB2 to ml-MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml-MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A-element substitution into the 3D Ti2ZnB2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li-ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors.
abstract: NA: Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system-level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure-property relationships across p-type, n-type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte-channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all-gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant-bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT-native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed-loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near-term direction for the field.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro-Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer.
abstract: NA: The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology-enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β-blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time-of-flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro-immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer-associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen-Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer-Macrocycle-Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture.
abstract: NA: The rational design of high-performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption-active motifs into higher-order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen-bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif-conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non-additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I3 - per molecule in the presence of a 100-fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif-level host-guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid-state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: Scalable and Lithography-Free Fabrication of High-Aspect-Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications.
abstract: NA: The scalable integration of low-dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography-free top-down etching approach to produce densely distributed high-aspect-ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single-crystal (SCD), and boron-doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2-inch wafer. By correlating time-dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag-initiated, redeposition-sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self-assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen-vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire-assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30-fold increase in electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl)-derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5-fold enhancement in pollutant-degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications.
abstract: NA: Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting-edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Autonomous Discovery of Multi-Material Metamaterials With Programmable Multimodal Thermal Responses via Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: NA: Inverse design deep learning models have significantly accelerated materials discovery through mapping complex structure-property relationships. However, they remain constrained by prohibitive data demands and are limited to in-distribution interpolation designs. Efficient out-of-distribution inverse design under sparse data constraints remains a critical bottleneck. Here we present an inverse design framework integrating Transformer encoder with reinforcement learning (RL) agent. By combining adaptable structural parameterization and hybrid iterative optimization, this framework efficiently navigates the complex, high-dimensional multi-material design landscape with extremely low data dependency (<103 samples). The inverse design framework leverages reward-driven mechanism to autonomously evolves multi-material architectures that achieve unseen target thermal deformation behaviors while strictly adhering to manufacturing requirements. Uniquely, the versatility of this framework is demonstrated through the realization of multiple thermal deformation targets, including near-zero, negative, and highly anisotropic thermal expansion, as well as complex multimodal deformations. Experimental validation of fabricated structures further confirms the efficacy of our framework for accelerated on-demand design of multi-material functional architectures.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single-Atom-Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth.
abstract: NA: Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite-free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single-atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single-atom-nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination-mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non-equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co-species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d-band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption-energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high-loading Li||LiFePO4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic-structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host-Guest Oxygen Reduction.
abstract: NA: Developing high-performance metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host-guest chemistry strategy based on metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular-level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O2. A series of fluorene-based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half-wave potential (E1/2, vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal-free COF-based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host-guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host-guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high-efficiency metal-free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto-Viscoelastic Patches.
abstract: NA: We report a machine learning (ML)-augmented magnetic sensing system for real-time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″-Fe16N2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML-based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical-grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real-time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous aluminum-based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic-anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni-Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high-surface-area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface-limited deposition. The resulting Al-alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge-transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric-cell operation and long-duration full-cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low-cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm-2. When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm-2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni-assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al-containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

title: Closed-Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy.
abstract: NA: Closed-loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed-schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real-time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed-loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed-loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof-of-concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next-generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.

title: Ultra-Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy.
abstract: NA: Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non-ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe-Co-Ni-Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m2) into the ferromagnetic face-centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non-magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am2/kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe-Si and Fe-Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high-performance soft magnetic alloys.

title: Electromigration-Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High-Carbon-Solubility Metals.
abstract: NA: Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8-10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating-current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the source. Raman mapping and ToF-SIMS profiling reveal 12C enrichment across source compositions from natural abundance to ∼88 at% 13C, with Raman-derived enrichment factors of 1.29-1.62. The composition dependence of these factors, with increased enrichment toward the 13C-rich end, supports isotope-sensitive transport coupled to localized precipitation. Finite-bias calculations demonstrate directional migration-barrier asymmetry, while isotope-dependent hopping and a concentration-threshold model predict preferential 12C enrichment in both hosts. Frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) measurements of both thermal conductivity components reveal a pronounced in-plane and a weaker out-of-plane composition dependence. These results show current-directed graphite formation in solid metals accompanied by isotope fractionation and composition-dependent thermal properties. This approach may extend to other mobile interstitial solutes in suitable metal hosts.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor-Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet-sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor-iridium coordination polymer (BTP-N-Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet-triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long-lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra-moiety excited (i-EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet-exciton transfer pathway with the i-EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: 4f-Electron-Regulated Dual-Periodic Bonding Evolution Across the Lanthanide Series.
abstract: NA: Lanthanide-based catalysts have attracted increasing attention due to their unique electronic structures, yet the relationship between 4f electron evolution and catalytic behavior remains unclear. Here, using structurally uniform lanthanide single-atom catalysts as a model platform, we systematically investigate the influence of 4f electron filling on bonding evolution across the lanthanide series. We reveal a dual-periodic trend in lanthanide-support binding energies and adsorbate bonding energies, which increases from La to Eu and from Gd to Yb. This behavior originates from progressive electron redistribution between 5d and 4f orbitals, which modulates the electron population of bonding orbitals. The half-filled 4f7 configuration induces an abrupt transition between Eu and Gd. Furthermore, similar crystal-field splitting enables robust linear relationships between binding and bonding energies across diverse coordination environments. More importantly, the persistence of these electronic characteristics across diverse coordination environments demonstrates that the dual-periodic evolution represents an intrinsic feature of lanthanide chemistry rather than a system-specific phenomenon. These findings establish a 4f-electron-regulated bonding framework for understanding lanthanide reactivity and guiding catalyst design.

title: Copper Surface Engineering Enables Uniform Zn Plating in Zn Batteries at Unity N/P Ratio.
abstract: NA: Zinc (Zn) metal plating is notoriously sensitive to interfacial inefficiencies under Zn-limited conditions, where small losses of active Zn rapidly lead to premature cell failure. Here, we demonstrate a surface reconstruction strategy for copper (Cu) current collectors that enables exceptional performance at a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.0. By chemically etching Cu to create a sacrificial cuprous chloride (γ-CuCl) interface, we obtained a micro-textured Cu substrate with increased electrochemical surface area (ECSA). Upon initial electrochemical reduction, γ-CuCl converts to metallic Cu while releasing Cl- ions into the local interfacial region of the electrolyte. Density functional theory calculations indicate that localized Cl- ions favorably regulate Zn2+ adsorption energy while suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. Benefitting from the synergistic combination of enhanced ECSA and dynamic Cl- mediated interfacial engineering, Zn//Cu cells achieve stable plating/stripping cycling for 1654 h (69 days). Notably, Zn//MnO2 full cells using 3D-printed etched Cu substrate assembled under a nominal N/P ratio of 1.0 (determined by a reversible capacity at 10 mA cm-2) deliver a remarkable device volumetric capacity of 53.5 mAh cm-3. Under high-rate cycling (80 mA cm-2), the cell retains 70% of initial capacity over 500 cycles. This performance represents a benchmark for Zn reversibility under extreme material-limited conditions.

title: In Situ Lab-on-Fiber Platform: A Versatile Tool for Dual-Mode Optoelectronic Tracking Photocorrosion Dynamics of Cadmium Sulfide.
abstract: NA: As versatile catalysts, metal sulfides (MSs) unlock new possibilities for photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, driving innovations in clean energy production. However, they are prone to photocorrosion under illumination, which severely impairs their catalytic efficiency and recyclability, thus fundamentally compromising the stability of the catalytic reaction system. Therefore, critical to this effort is the elucidation of photocorrosion for the practical application of high-performance catalysts and long-lasting reactors. Herein, a lab-on-fiber sensing platform is developed for in situ, real-time monitoring of the photocorrosion of cadmium sulfide (CdS). Anchored by a tapered seven-core optical fiber, the platform facilitates dual-mode sensing by correlating transmission spectrum evolution with photocurrent dynamics, revealing that CdS photocorrosion exhibits a nonlinear dependence on light intensity. The photocorrosion rate is minimized at 0.8 mW∙cm-2 UV light and is further suppressed by applying a 0.4 V bias. Furthermore, the platform uncovers a protective, dynamic sulfur cycle enabled by sacrificial agents on the catalyst surface. Crucially, key structure-activity relationships of the CdS undergoing photocorrosion are established, enabling the optimization of catalysts and reactors. Beyond catalytic systems, the platform is applicable to the operando exploration of interfacial dynamic behaviors and mechanisms in various nanomaterials, thereby underpinning the design of micro-nano material interfaces and reaction systems.

title: Mechanically-Driven Reconstruction of Lithium Metal for Stable All-Solid-State Batteries.
abstract: NA: Dendrite growth at lithium-metal anode remains a critical bottleneck in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Current approaches often rely on alloy anodes that compromise energy density or artificial interlayers, introducing additional processing complexity. Herein, we show that accumulated deformation imposed by repeated folding and rolling mechanically reconstructs commercial Li from surface to bulk, replacing a rough carbonate-rich surface and mixed texture with a refined oxide-passivated surface and a strongly Li(200)-preferred texture. At low and medium folding degrees, surface refinement and renewal of the native passivation layer improve solid-solid contact and interfacial Li-ion transport, but remain insufficient to prevent short circuiting, whereas high-degree reconstruction drives texture homogenization, reduces spatial variations in local interfacial response, and synchronizes Li recession and advancement across the rigid Li | solid-state electrolyte interface. The synchronous interface motion suppresses differential recession and void formation during stripping, while mitigating dendritic Li growth during plating. As a result, Li | LPSCl1.5 | NMC811 full cells achieve 79.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at C/2 rate, support 7.4 mA h cm-2 operation with 0.05% decay per cycle, and cycle stably below 0.5 MPa. These findings establish mechanical reconstruction as a direct materials-level strategy for stabilizing Li metal in sulfide-based ASSBs.

title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration.
abstract: NA: Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment-degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@LabPC, which self-assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular-weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans (C. albicans) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection-dysbiosis-recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.

title: Magnetically-Gated Haptic Locomotion Display Enabled by Motion-Coupled Light Emission.
abstract: NA: Magnetic actuation is a powerful strategy in robotics for tactile feedback, navigation, and biomedical applications and can be extended to interactive displays by coupling mechanical motion with optical emission. Here, we present a magnetically-gated haptic locomotion display (MHLD) that integrates a flexible alternating-current (AC)-driven quantum-dot light-emitting diode (QLED) with a magnetoresponsive elastomeric soft actuator. Under external magnetic fields, the soft actuator deforms and modulates its contact with the AC display, triggering electroluminescence (EL) whose emission area and intensity are directly coupled to mechanical displacement. A maximum luminance of 396 cd m- 2 was achieved, with emission area and intensity varying with deformation. The device maintains stable output under repeated actuation, with directional motion programmable via magnetization profiles. Demonstrations include a 3 × 3 haptic feedback array visualizing pixel displacement and a maze-navigating locomotive display with path-dependent emission. Finite element simulations support the contact-mediated formation of the vertical electric field underlying motion-coupled light emission.

title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali-Ion Batteries Through Two-Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering.
abstract: NA: Carbon-based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C60 has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g-1 than the traditional graphite anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs).
