However, its zero-dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali-metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal-free two-dimensional C60 covalent network (2D-C60) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP-2D-C60) and hexagonal phase (HP-2D-C60) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C60 molecule. TP-2D-C60 delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g-1 at 0.1 A g-1, outperforming HP-2D-C60 (408.6 mAh g-1) and pristine C60 (3.4 mAh g-1). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP-2D-C60 exhibits a higher density of Li-ion binding sites and a lower Li-ion migration barrier than HP-2D-C60. To assess its universality across ion-battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP-2D-C60 as an anode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g-1 at 0.1 A g-1.

title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster-Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature.
abstract: NA: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three-dimensional cuprous iodide cluster-based covalent organic framework (CuI-MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI-MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti-interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density-functional theory calculations reveal that the imine-linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption-desorption sites, while the electron-rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on-chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti-interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high-performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster-based COFs in gas sensing.

title: Bacteria-Trained, MnO2-Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy.
abstract: NA: Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on-target off-tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell-based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform-trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO2 nanoparticles (designated MnArmL-trDCs)-endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano-transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO2 armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC-II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS-STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor-draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL-trDCs induce a pro-inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti-PD-1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano-engineering cell armor-based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π-π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF-based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre-synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS-treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long-term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.

title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000-Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate.
abstract: NA: Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (Ol) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal-oxygen bonds that restrict Ol migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg2V1.33O4 catalyst with Rhδ +─Ov─Vn + interfacial sites (n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi-metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm-2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rhδ +─Ov─Vn + ⇌ Rhδ +─Ol─V( n +1)+), which endows the catalyst with effective Ol migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking-resistant CH3O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long-term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state-of-the-art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol gRh -1 h-1 for H2 and CO, respectively, along with a light-to-chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi-metallic, redox-active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable Ol-mediated photothermal catalysis.

title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS-Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression.
abstract: NA: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)-mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS-eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non-canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD-knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS-mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.

title: Processing Window Expansion Enables Uniform Crystallization in Scalable Ambient-Fabricated Perovskite Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: Slot-die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition-to-annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot-die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ-to-α phase transition while suppressing non-photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large-grained α-FAPbI3 films with minimized vertical compositional gradient and reduced residual strain. The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy-level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large-area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS-L-3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Correction to "MoS2@Polyaniline for Aqueous Ammonium-Ion Supercapacitors".
Threo-Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo-chiral cation additive of (2S,3R)-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl‑induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral‑center threo‑configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically‑favored parallel‑to‑lattice multi‑site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective "lock-and-key" interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm2 large-area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS-D-2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high-efficiency and ultra-stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Heterointerfacial Bonding Governs Service Stability in Flexible Perovskite Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: The service stability of flexible perovskite solar module (FPSM) is contingent upon the bonding strength and stress-response behavior at heterointerfaces. However, the fullerene-based layer mainly relies on weak non-covalent interactions. This makes it difficult for the FPSM to tackle the challenges posed by the coupling of multiple stresses in the actual service environment. Through the blending strategy of the polyamide curing agent and fullerene derivatives, we constructed an active energy-dissipating multi-bond network featuring covalent bond anchoring and hydrogen bond dissipation, which significantly enhanced the interfacial bonding and energy dissipation capabilities. Based on this strategy, a 100 cm2 FPSM achieves a recorded power conversion efficiency of 22.33% (certified 21.5%). More importantly, for the first time, we developed an in situ bending electroluminescence experiment for FPSM under ultraviolet irradiation. After 5000 consecutive bending cycles, there was no significant decline in the module's performance, which verified its service stability under multi-field coupling.

title: Spin-State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion.
abstract: NA: Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon-free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber-Bosch process is energy-intensive and emits substantial CO2. Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived Co3O4 electrocatalyst (MD-Co3O4) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co-MOF-74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability for the electrosynthesis of NH3 from nitrate, along with robust activity over a wide pH and nitrate concentration range. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the oxygen vacancies generated during MOF pyrolysis induce coordination distortion of octahedral Co sites, leading to a high-spin state transition with an electron-rich configuration that synergistically enhances nitrate adsorption and interfacial electron transfer, thereby boosting the intrinsic activity. Moreover, this MOF-based strategy is applicable to other M1Co2O4 spinels, which provides an effective approach for spin engineering at the atomic scale and sustainable ammonia synthesis.

title: Monolithically 3D-Printed Spectral-Spatial Meta-Authenticators.
abstract: NA: Metasurface holography can encode multiple independent images in a single flat element, yet simultaneous operation at several visible wavelengths has typically relied on geometric-phase elements, which require a prescribed circular polarization and bulky polarization optics, and on high-index dielectrics that can suffer from visible-band absorption. Here, we demonstrate a monolithically 3D-printed, low-index, height-coded metasurface that performs polarization-insensitive, broadband holography across spectral (wavelength) and spatial (near- and far-field) channels. The propagation phase accumulated by each resin pillar is set by its height, so a single height map fixes the phase response at every wavelength at once and acts as a multi-wavelength phase library. The symmetric pillar cross-section removes the dependence on input polarization, and the transparent resin keeps the response low-loss across the visible band. A fabrication-aware optimization folds the discrete height levels imposed by two-photon-lithography slicing directly into the loss, so the design is printed as optimized in a single continuous step, without post-optimization rounding. Experimentally, the device reconstructs a far-field image that is read directly as a public key together with wavelength- and distance-selective near-field images that act as locked passwords, realizing a compact, dual-credential optical authentication scheme under unpolarized illumination without polarization optics.

title: Activation-Free and Strain-Resilient Island-Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine-Learning-Enabled Epidermal Electromyography.
abstract: NA: Liquid metal particle-based inks offer a scalable route toward stretchable electronics, yet their practical implementation is hindered by activation-dependent conductivity and poor electrical stability under deformation. Herein, we report an intrinsically conductive and strain-resilient liquid metal ink with a rationally engineered island-bridge micro-architecture, in which Cu-decorated carbon nanotubes (CuCNTs) bridge adjacent liquid metal particles (LMPs) through initial hydrogen-bonding/coordination-assisted attachment to the native gallium-oxide shell, followed by local Cu-Ga alloying at the CuCNTs/LMPs interface. Enabled by solvent-mediated dispersion and interfacial hybridization, the strain-resilient composite ink supports high-resolution (100 µm) screen printing and deformable circuit integration. The dynamically reconfigurable island-bridge network retains a sheet resistance of 1.3 × 10-1 Ω sq-1 at 300% strain, together with stable resistance during prolonged cyclic stretching and bending. When printed into a compact 12-channel array on breathable fibrous substrates, the resulting electrode array exhibits low skin-electrode impedance and superior high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) performance compared with commercial gel electrodes. Combined with machine-learning-assisted analysis, the electromyography arrays enable training-state recognition, individualized load assessment, and continuous monitoring of fatigue-associated exercise states during dynamic exercise. This work provides a scalable strategy for intrinsically conductive liquid metal electronics and advances their application in intelligent wearable biointerfaces and soft electronic systems.

title: Adaptive Supramolecular Interactions Govern Redox-Active Molecules in Aqueous Redox Flow Batteries.
abstract: NA: Weak noncovalent interactions critically govern molecular behavior in solution, yet how they shape redox processes in aqueous electrochemical environments remains underexplored. Here, we demonstrate control over the solubility and redox stability of aromatic redox-active molecules in aqueous redox flow batteries (RFBs). Zwitterionic substitution of naphthalene diimide (NDI) bearing quaternary ammonium and sulfonate groups shows weak π-π cohesion through steric and electrostatic effects, rendering otherwise insoluble NDIs responsive to external anions. Hydrophobic and weakly hydrated anions such as iodide and bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide disrupt residual stacking through anion-π interactions, enabling dissolution to concentrations approaching 1.3 M. Upon electrochemical reduction, these anions dissociate, and the reduced NDI species are instead stabilized through spin pairing and cation-mediated intermolecular interactions, which suppress irreversible aggregation, slow self-discharge, and enable rapid redox reactions. Operando Raman spectroscopy, 1H NMR, and EPR elucidate the redox-state-dependent evolution of these supramolecular assemblies. Together, these results establish zwitterionic molecular design for adaptive supramolecular redox chemistry in aqueous RFBs.

title: Time-Encoded Ligand Presentation via a Magnetically Actuated Hydrogel Mitigates T Cell Exhaustion.
abstract: NA: Adoptive T cell therapy (ACT) requires ex vivo expansion of tumor-reactive CD8+ T cells, yet prolonged antigenic stimulation frequently induces exhaustion, limiting persistence and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we present a magnetically actuated, extracellular matrix-mimetic hydrogel that enables reversible control of T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation timing. By embedding αCD3ε/αCD28-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles within a soft hyaluronic acid matrix, external magnetic fields dynamically expose or conceal stimulatory ligands, allowing programmable alternation between activation and rest. Continuous ligand presentation sustains TCR signaling and drives inhibitory receptor expression and functional exhaustion. In contrast, alternating activation-rest cycles periodically attenuate proximal TCR signaling, reduce exhaustion-associated marker expression, and bias differentiation toward central memory-like states while preserving cytokine production and recall capacity. T cells expanded under intermittent stimulation exhibit enhanced antigen-specific cytotoxicity, reduced dependence on PD-1 blockade, and superior tumor control in vivo, together with increased CD8+ T cell abundance across analyzed tissues. These results identify temporal control of mechanochemical signaling as a materials-encoded regulator of T cell fate and provide a non-genetic strategy for generating functionally competent T cell products with reduced exhaustion-associated dysfunction and improved antitumor activity.

title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration.
abstract: NA: Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep-seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug-resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self-propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic-gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3-guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo-responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature-dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail-safe thermal self-destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface-engineered (DSS)6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone-homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo-immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next-generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro-engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

title: Lewis-Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries.
abstract: NA: Alkaline all-iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low-cost grid-scale energy storage using Earth-abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer-sphere electron-transfer kinetics of Fe-chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)-region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis-basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe-chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide-assisted outer-sphere electron-transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni3S4-modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm-2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm-2, compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm-2 for the pristine cell. The Ni3S4-based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm-2. This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis-basic interface engineering as a strategy for high-power and low-cost long-duration energy storage.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large-Area Tin-based Perovskite Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p-type small molecule, 4,4'-(5,6-bis(2-methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole-4,7-diyl)bis(2,5-difluoro-N,N-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic-angle spinning 1H NMR, 1H-1H double-quantum-single-quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning-rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high-quality Sn-based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap-assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG-PEDOT:PSS-based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1-cm2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04-cm2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N2 atmosphere.

title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard-Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion-Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity.
abstract: NA: Sodium-ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard-carbon anode design lacks a precursor-level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed-pore formation. Here we establish a precursor-level cohesion-solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene-fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke-like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard-carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect-engineered carbon galleries. The solvent-selected AHC-80-1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g-1 at 0.05 A g-1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide-temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at -20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10-kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC-80-1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg-1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC-80-1400 production reduces climate-change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor-stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb-Ru/RuO2 to Break the Activity-Stability Trade-Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution.
abstract: NA: Developing highly active and stable Ru-based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru-based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb-doped Ru/RuO2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site-Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen-intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb-Ru/RuO2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm-2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm-2. This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low-cost PEMWE hydrogen production.

title: A Glycan Key Unlocks Microglia Targeting and Reprogramming to Promote Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: NA: Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers uncontrolled neuroinflammation driven by dysfunctional microglia and pro-inflammatory-biased reprogramming, yet precise therapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we report a novel glycan-targeted nanoparticle system (ICT@APD) designed to enhance the microglia-reprogramming potential of icaritin (ICT) while overcoming its inherent narrow therapeutic window. By functionalizing nanoparticles with 2,5-anhydro-D-mannitol (2,5-AM), a high-affinity ligand for the microglia-specific transporter GLUT5, ICT@APD achieves selective microglial uptake and amplifies the capacity of ICT to reprogram microglia toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. The targeted reprogramming consequently creates a positive microenvironment that promotes axon regeneration, neuronal survival, and synaptic reconstruction, leading to significantly improved locomotor recovery after SCI. Our findings establish a novel glycan-mediated microglial targeting and reprogramming strategy for SCI repair, which may extend to other central nervous system disorders and provide a referenceable platform for the delivery of other therapeutic agents with a narrow therapeutic window.

title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low-Cost Solar Fuels.
abstract: NA: Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field-scale NP typically operates at sub-percent solar-to-biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double-digit solar-to-fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar-to-chemical conversion.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal-Organic Network for CO2 Conversion.
abstract: NA: Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous-phase synthesis of a woven metal-organic superstructure assembled from Cu2+ and 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene-1,3,5-triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu2+ yields charged one-dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two-dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π-conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox-active Cu2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu-TNPG network was evaluated for visible-light-driven CO2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu-TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre-activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H2, highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu-Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C-C Coupling for Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethylene.
abstract: NA: The abundant Cu0/Cuδ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C-C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuOx. The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene at -1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm-2 in a flow cell. In-situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cuδ+ (0<δ<1) sites at multimetallic interfaces is effectively regulated by other metals, inducing electronic heterogeneity and an asymmetric charge distribution on the Cu sites that facilitates asymmetric *CO-*CHO coupling. This work establishes the design principles for Cu-based multimetallic alloy with atomic-level customisation, demonstrating that the precise structural design and electronic structure of Cuδ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.

title: Anti-Poisoning Tin Single-Atom Unlocks High-Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction.
abstract: NA: The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru-based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active-site blockage by adsorbed species. Herein, we report a Sn-doped RuO2@Ru catalyst supported on carbon black, wherein atomically dispersed Sn modulates the electronic structure of RuO2 via Sn─O bonds, simultaneously facilitating water dissociation, optimizing *H adsorption, and preventing *OH poisoning. The catalyst achieves exceptional performance with an overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm-2, positioning it among the most active HER catalysts reported to date. When integrated into a full AEMWE, it operates at 1.85 V and 1000 mA cm-2 with stability exceeding 300 h. Mechanistic studies suggest that Sn doping fine-tunes the *OH and *H binding energies, addressing the kinetic imbalance inherent in conventional Ru catalysts. This work highlights the effectiveness of atomic-level electronic engineering via an anti-poisoning strategy for designing efficient, stable alkaline HER electrocatalysts toward industrial hydrogen production.

title: Engineering Thermoelectric-Electrocatalytic Coupling in RuO2/PrCoO3 Heterointerface for Efficient Oxygen Evolution.
abstract: NA: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is pivotal for diverse electrochemical energy conversion systems; however, it has so far been plagued by sluggish kinetics and excessive energy consumption. In this study, we proposed an innovative thermoelectric-electrocatalytic coupling strategy to enhance OER efficiency by constructing an Ohmic heterointerface through uniform integration of RuO2 with thermoelectric oxide (PrCoO3). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the thermoelectric potential generated by PrCoO3 selectively activates the intrinsically inert (101) facet of RuO2 by lowering *OOH formation barrier, thereby substantially boosting the overall OER performance. Consequently, the RuO2/PrCoO3 heterointerface delivered exceptional OER performance under a mild temperature gradient (ΔT) of 175°C, achieving dramatic reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm-2 from 300 mV (ΔT = 0°C) to 178 mV, 4 300% increase in current density, and negligible potential loss over 1,000 h. When the catalyst was assembled into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the cell driven by spontaneous heating reached a low voltage of 2.18 V at a current density of 2.0 A cm-2, with stable operation for 600 h. These insights into harnessing thermal gradient via integrated electrocatalytic system are crucial for the recovery of industrial waste heat and its conversion into high-value chemicals.

title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications.
abstract: NA: Rare earth-proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE3+) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE3+, enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth-protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.

title: A Novel pH-Activatable Nanozyme for Treating Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis by Regulating Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and the Tumor Microenvironment.
abstract: NA: Multi-omics analyses implicate enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in breast cancer bone metastasis (BCBM). To target this metabolic vulnerability, we develop SPMMPA, a bone-targeted nanozyme comprising a Prussian blue core, a disulfide-bridged mesoporous silica interlayer, and a manganese oxide shell, functionalized with polyethylenimine, alendronate, and the Ser-Asp-Ser-Ser-Asp peptide. Its acid-enhanced catalytic activity promotes reactive oxygen species production and glutathione depletion, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced OXPHOS and adenosine triphosphate production, and downregulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha. Alendronate and silicon release contribute to reduced osteoclast activity and preservation of bone structure. Near-infrared irradiation further enhances treatment efficacy through photothermal heating below 48°C. In mouse models of BCBM, SPMMPA suppresses tumor growth and alleviates osteolysis, without overt toxicity in the assays performed. These findings support a pH-responsive catalytic strategy that couples disruption of tumor energy metabolism with protection of bone homeostasis.

title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress-ROS-Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy.
abstract: NA: In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-ROS-inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress-centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER-regulating heterojunction (ERR-HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti3C2 MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti3C2 heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H2O2 to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK-CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue-regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR-HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self-perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection-associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress-ROS-inflammation cycle inhibition.

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow-Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition.
abstract: NA: Neuromorphic in-sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co-localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation-anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion-migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo-modulation is further attenuated by exciton-polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion-migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3-(1-vinyl-3-imidazolyl)-propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro- and photo-synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation-anion pair prevents long-distance ion-migration, ensuring strong cation-anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi-wavelength photo-synaptic modulation coupled with electro-synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application-relevant in-sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color-guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian-speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing-computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.

title: Engineered Excited-State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators.
abstract: NA: Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low-cost, high-performance x-ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu-I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin-orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x-ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation-induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation-state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu-I clusters with nearly identical x-ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited-state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water-resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV-1 and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm-1. Furthermore, tandem integration with a high-Z scintillator enables selective density-discriminating x-ray imaging and micro-computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high-throughput development of promising metal-cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes.
abstract: NA: Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high-performance perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next-generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs4PbBr6 phase often accompanies CsPbBr3 crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive-mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3-carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3-CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr3 formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr3 phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs4PbBr6 phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual-Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion.
abstract: NA: Rational design of dual-site catalysts to decouple complex multi-electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO3 -) reduction reaction (NO3RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co7Fe3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO3RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4-electron step reduces NO3 - to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4-electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4-electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well-defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co7Fe3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO3RR through synergistic dual-spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h-1 cm-2 at -0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn-nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm-2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.

title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications.
abstract: NA: AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next-generation ferroelectric in-memory computing architecture and radio-frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high-quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system-level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy-efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Quantification of Magnetic Interactions in van der Waals Heterostructures Using Lorentz Transmission Electron Microscopy and Off-Axis Electron Holography.
abstract: NA: Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials are promising for memory and logic applications because of their tunable magnetic properties and compatibility with vdW heterostructure devices. However, coupling between magnetic textures in stacked layers is difficult to resolve in conventional plan-view measurements because the magnetic signal is integrated over the sample thickness. Here, these interactions are quantified in Fe3GeTe2 (FGT)/graphite/FGT heterostructures using cross-sectional Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and off-axis electron holography, enabling reconstruction of the local projected magnetic induction within and between the layers. Domain alignment weakens with increasing FGT separation, yielding a stray-field coupling length scale of λ=37±7  nm for the cross-sectional geometry studied here, corresponding to the average separation at which domain misalignment first emerges. This length scale corresponds to an approximately 23% reduction in the interlayer magnetic induction relative to bulk FGT. The magnetic induction is reduced relative to bulk FGT up to ∼ 100 nm from a surface. Comparisons with model-based iterative reconstructions of the magnetization and micromagnetic simulations show that this near-surface reduction is due to demagnetizing and stray fields. These results quantify the magnetic induction in stacked vdW magnets and guide the design of devices that require controllable coupling between magnetic textures.

title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half-Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta3N5 via Cocatalyst Engineering.
abstract: NA: Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half-reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5 remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoOx cocatalyst is developed via a multi-step incipient wetness impregnation strategy. The optimized Pt@Cr2O3/Ta3N5/RuCoOx achieves stoichiometric pure water splitting with an apparent quantum yield of 0.72% at 420 nm, representing the highest value reported for Ta-based nitride/oxynitride photocatalysts to date. Mechanistic studies reveal that an enhanced interfacial electric field facilitates hole extraction, while a reduced formation barrier of key intermediates accelerates surface reaction kinetics, thereby overcoming the long-standing bottleneck in photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta3N5. This work establishes cocatalyst compatibility as a key design consideration for stable photocatalytic pure water splitting and provides mechanistic insight for the rational design of advanced nitride and oxynitride photocatalysts.

title: Synergistic Interaction Engineering Enables Homogeneous Mixed-Cation Perovskite Single Crystals for High-Performance X-Ray Detection.
abstract: NA: Mixed A-site compositions are an effective route to boost the x-ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single-crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid-enabled synergistic interaction-engineering strategy for growing phase-homogeneous mixed-cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium-rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium-rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x-ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 106 µC Gy-1 cm-2, a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s-1, and excellent operational stability. This kinetic-regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed-cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low-dose, high-performance optoelectronic devices.

title: Shear Alignment Polymer Extrusion 3D Printing of High-Loading Nanocomposites With Long-Range Ordered Nanostructures.
abstract: NA: Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three-dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable fabrication of macroscopic nanocomposites with complex 3D architectures. A key advancement is the development of high-loading filaments (e.g., 55 wt% BN in polylactic acid) and a high-shear extrusion system, overcoming the traditional challenges of poor processability and structural integrity in high-filler composites. Post-sintering yields pure nanomaterial architectures that fully replicate the 3D printed geometry with zero volume shrinkage and exceptional thermomechanical stability-withstanding temperatures above the polymer melting and decomposition without structural failure. These materials exhibit tailored functionalities: vertically aligned BN composites show enhanced thermal conductivity (1.07 W/m/K); horizontally aligned BN structures offer efficient thermal insulation (0.071 W/m/K); and BN membranes display robust mechanical performance (a compressive strength of 3.4 MPa). Generalizable to diverse nanomaterials (0D to 2D), SHAPE opens new avenues for cross-scale design in thermal management, energy storage, and advanced structural materials.

title: Constructing Stretchable Superhydrophobic Perovskite Quantum Dot Films via Dual-Phase Synergistic Engineering.
abstract: NA: Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) films intended for flexible optical applications are required not only to exhibit excellent luminescence performance, but also to simultaneously possess high stretchability, superhydrophobicity, patterned luminescence, and multicolor programmability under complex conditions such as large deformation, liquid intrusion, and long-term service. Here we propose a dual-phase synergistic engineering strategy, and in combination with replica molding and femtosecond laser direct writing technologies, achieve the construction of a biomimetic superhydrophobic surface and the controllable precipitation of PQDs while endowing the film with superelasticity. Benefiting from the dual-phase structure and biomimetic surface design, the film still retains more than 52% of its initial luminescence intensity and a water contact angle above 150° under 800% tensile deformation. This strategy is applicable to full-spectrum luminescent systems spanning 470-688 nm and supports proof-of-concept binary optical encoding. After continuous immersion in water for 240 days, the film still retains more than 90% of its initial luminescence intensity and more than 95% machine-learning recognition accuracy. This work provides a new strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible PQDs films with stable luminescence under deformation and water exposure.

title: Cesium Tin Iodide Perovskites Engineer the Sn4+/Sn2+ Redox Reaction in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: Tin displays rich redox chemistry transitioning between metallic tin (Sn0), stannous (Sn2+), and stannic (Sn4+) states, among which the Sn4+/Sn2+ couple offers the highest theoretical potential ( >0.14 V vs. SHE) whereas remaining unrealized in practical batteries. Herein, we introduce the in situ and successive growth of CsSnI3 single perovskite and Cs2SnI6 double perovskite layers on the cathode surface during operation, enabling the first demonstration of the Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction in zinc-ion batteries, with an increased potential to 0.39 V versus SHE due to enhanced tin-halide coordination. Further integrated into Zn||SnCl4 full batteries, the design delivers dual discharge plateaus at 1.18 V (Sn4+/Sn2+) and 1.28 V (I0/I-), yielding a high areal capacity of 0.80 mAh cm-2 at 1 mA cm-2 and high energy density of 0.99 mWh cm-2 (660 Wh kg-1, per SnCl4·5H2O mass of the cathode). The three-electron transfer design exhibits considerable longevity, with Swagelok cells retaining 7000 cycles at 16 mA cm-2 and pouch cells sustaining 200 cycles at 4 mA cm-2 without capacity loss. By enabling the high-potential Sn4+/Sn2+ redox reaction, the perovskite interlayer provides a cross-disciplinary strategy to advancing high-energy aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta-Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication.
abstract: NA: Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta-window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8-13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid-infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external-source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible-laser-infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof-of-concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors.
abstract: NA: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state-centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history-dependent state trajectories. A problem-specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion-specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden-state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy-storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical-state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

title: Machine-Learning-Potential-Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes.
abstract: NA: Ionic transport in solid-state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large-scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum-level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale-accuracy gap in halide-tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl-/Br- ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP-driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl-enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br- enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion-engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP-enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid-state materials.

title: Grain-Boundary-Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity-Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing.
abstract: NA: Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity-tolerant catalytic H2 sensor based on a grain-boundary-rich palladium nanostructure (PdGB) that operates without any external heating. The PdGB sensor functions reliably at 22°C-80°C and 0%-90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m-3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000-fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H2), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine-learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature-programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdHx formation for weakening H2O adsorption and suppress humidity-induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials-design strategy for next-generation humidity-tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah-Level Aqueous Ammonium-Ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π-π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8-tetraamino-5,10-dihydrophenazine-1,4,6,9-tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m2 g-1, delivers 242.8 mAh g-1 at 0.1 A g-1, and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR-FTIR and EQCM-D measurements reveal that NH4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H3O+ for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe-PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g-1. Moreover, the first Ah-level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300-Cycle Ah-Level Anode-Free Sodium Batteries.
abstract: NA: Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode-targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode-specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)-dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record-high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg- 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode-free full cells based on Na4Fe3(PO4)2 (NFPP), Na3V2(PO4)3 (NVP), and NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

title: Engineering Bidirectional Neuromodulation: A Review of Neural Excitation and Inhibition Technologies.
abstract: NA: Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. Yet neural activity can require regulation in opposing directions across different cellular, circuit and pathological states, motivating bidirectional neuromodulation that can both enhance and suppress neural activity. In this review, we examine the mechanisms and technologies that enable such bidirectional control across electrical, optical, thermal, mechanical, magnetic and chemical modalities. We compare these approaches in terms of spatiotemporal performance, penetration depth, specificity and safety, and examine the materials, transduction strategies and device architectures used to implement bidirectional neural control. We further discuss the applications of bidirectional neuromodulation in neuroscience research and the treatment of neurological disorders. Finally, we discuss the technical challenges and future directions toward more precise, independent and integrated bidirectional control, including its extension to closed-loop adaptive regulation.

title: Ultrasound-Activated Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework Synergistically Enhances Antitumor Immunity by Epigenetic Reprogramming and Pyroptosis Induction.
abstract: NA: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory form of cell death, elicits robust antitumor immune responses. However, pyroptosis-based cancer immunotherapy is hampered by the epigenetic silencing of gasdermin E (GSDME) through hypermethylation of the DFNA5 gene. To overcome this limitation, we engineered an innovative nanosystem by first synthesizing a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive decitabine prodrug (DTO), which was subsequently encapsulated within hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks to form the HDTO nanoplatform. Upon ultrasound (US) activation, the HDTO nanoplatform exhibited potent ROS generation, enabling two complementary functions: (1) triggering decitabine release to demethylate DFNA5 and restore GSDME expression and (2) activating caspase-3, thereby initiating the caspase-3/GSDME-mediated pyroptotic pathway. This apoptosis-to-pyroptosis switching mechanism significantly enhanced immunogenic cell death and potentiated antitumor immunity. In vivo studies demonstrated that US-activated HDTO induced robust pyroptosis, remodeled the tumor microenvironment, and elicited superior antitumor immune responses, resulting in marked suppression of tumor growth and metastasis. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that HDTO + US-induced pyroptosis depleted nonimmune cells while expanding monocyte and neutrophil populations, demonstrating effective immunoreprogramming. This study establishes a novel therapeutic paradigm that synergistically integrates epigenetic modulation with pyroptosis induction to enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Self-Segregated Buried-Interface Regulation Resolves Kinetic-Environmental Coupling for Ambient Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Ambient fabrication of flexible perovskite solar cells is fundamentally limited by a detrimental kinetic-environmental coupling at the buried interface, where moisture ingress and nonoptimal crystallization mutually compromise film quality-yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using dual-side in situ photoluminescence, we overturn the conventional top-down model by revealing simultaneous nucleation at both gas-liquid and liquid-solid interfaces during antisolvent-assisted solution processing, but find that outward solvent evaporation delays α-phase conversion at the buried interface relative to the surface, creating kinetic mismatch that exacerbates moisture attack and defect accumulation. To address these kinetic and environmental constraints, we design a self-segregating multifunctional molecule, 2-[(3-trifluoromethyl)phenyl]amino-3-pyridinecarboxylic acid (NFA), which spontaneously enriches at the buried interface to synchronize dual-interface crystallization while simultaneously passivating defects, optimizing energy-level alignment, and constructing a hydrophobic barrier against moisture ingress. Consequently, this self-segregated kinetic-environmental regulation yields record ambient flexible photovoltaic performance with power-conversion efficiencies of 24.84% (0.09 cm2, certified at 23.75%) and 21.46% on mini-modules (13.8 cm2). The optimized devices maintain 96.26% of their starting efficiency following 1000 h damp aging at 85 ± 5% RH. Our work establishes self-segregated interfacial regulation as a rational route to address kinetic and environmental constraints in scalable flexible photovoltaics.

title: GaSex Nanoparticles Modulate Neutrophil Function and Mitigate NET-Driven Osteogenic Impairment in Osteomyelitis Therapy.
abstract: NA: Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis-associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in Prkn-knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium-selenium nanoparticles (GaSex) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET-driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair-limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSex as a redox-regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.

title: Decoupling Protection and Doping Unlocks Asymmetric Zn Single Atoms for Efficient Oxygen Reduction.
abstract: NA: Precise manipulation of the coordination environment in single-atom catalysts is crucial yet challenging for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Here we present a sacrificial-guided etching strategy to activate intrinsically passive d10 Zn centers in single-atom catalysts, wherein Bi(NO3)3-mediated protection preserves ZnN4 coordination by mitigating excessive etching, while NaCl-driven Cl doping imparts a remote electron-withdrawing effect, concertedly modulating the electronic structure of the Zn centers. This decoupling strategy, which assigns protection and doping to distinct species, unlocks asymmetric Zn single atoms with dual precision over coordination number and dopant configuration. The resulting catalyst achieves an exceptional ORR half-wave potential of 0.916 V, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and delivers a record peak power density of 258 mW cm-2 with outstanding cycling stability exceeding 450 h in zinc-air batteries. Integrated theoretical and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that Cl incorporation disrupts the symmetric ZnN4 electronic structure, optimizes the d-band center, and alters unoccupied orbital hybridization, thereby accelerating O2 protonation and boosting the overall catalytic activity. This work establishes a well-defined strategy for the precise construction of single-atom metal centers, providing insights into the development of high-performance non-precious metal electrocatalysts.

title: Hollow Conjugated Microporous Polymers Anchored With ZnxCd1-xS Quantum Dots: An Additive-Free Photocatalyst for H2O2 Synthesis via S-Scheme Charge Transfer.
abstract: NA: Photocatalytic H2O2 production via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR) offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, but single-component photocatalysts suffer from rapid charge recombination. Here, we construct an S-scheme heterojunction by growing ZnxCd1-xS (ZCS) quantum dots (QDs) in situ on hollow conjugated microporous polymers (CMPs) containing selenadiazole units (hPSe). The hollow CMPs scaffold provides high surface area, abundant pores for QDs embedding, efficient mass transfer, and enhanced light harvesting, while the selenadiazole units promote strong interfacial coupling. In pure water without any sacrificial agent, the optimal ZCS@hPSe-2 composite achieved an outstanding H2O2 production rate of 15.13 mmol g-1 h-1 with a synergy factor of 1.53 and an apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 8.82% at 400 nm, operating exclusively via the 2e- ORR. The dramatic performance is attributed to the S-scheme charge transfer mechanism, which preserves the strong redox potentials of both components and suppresses bulk charge recombination. This work demonstrates that rational integration of QDs with hollow CMPs provides a viable pathway toward efficient, additive-free photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis.

title: Design of Bridging-Oxygen-Modulated Fe-Ni Dual-Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc-Air Batteries.
abstract: NA: Rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts.
