The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface.
abstract: NA: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: A case study in conflicts of interest.
Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival.
abstract: NA: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich's ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis.
abstract: NA: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium-derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes.
abstract: NA: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning-assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth-based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
abstract: NA: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe.
abstract: NA: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g-wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity.
abstract: NA: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs.
abstract: NA: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas, the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS. However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter (SOPT) and S locus glycine-rich protein (SGRP), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana. Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness.
abstract: NA: At the skin's surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E2, which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2.
abstract: NA: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF2. This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

title: It's not perfect-but it's me.
Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error.
abstract: NA: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun's arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning.
abstract: NA: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm.
abstract: NA: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension-the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as "Least Concern" on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum.
abstract: NA: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting.
abstract: NA: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: When AI takes away the thrill of discovery.
abstract: NA: "Pure math is being devastated or revolutionized, depending on your point of view." So said Cornell professor Steven Strogatz after the artificial intelligence (AI) company OpenAI announced in early September a potential solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize problems that represent the highest goals for mathematical proofs. OpenAI's solution involved unleashing an army of AI agents at a cost of millions of dollars in computing power, and it also certainly drew on decades of human effort in mathematics before it. Then a few weeks later, OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts describing progress on 372 mathematical problem families, and Google DeepMind published (in Science) solutions from their own AI math system. These events are potentially exciting for those who long to know the answers to these problems as soon as possible, but they have also sent the world of mathematics reeling, and pose an even bigger question for all fields: Can the satisfaction of understanding ever replace the thrill of discovery?

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars' early crust and mantle.
abstract: NA: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet's geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars' surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice.
abstract: NA: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals.
abstract: NA: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°-twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

title: India needs a tree conservation plan.
Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain.
abstract: NA: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows (Corvus corone) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

title: Dynamic functionality-enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels.
abstract: NA: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal.
abstract: NA: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd5AlI2, a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd5AlI2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer.
abstract: NA: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death.
abstract: NA: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation-induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting.
abstract: NA: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter's states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra-unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models.
abstract: NA: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules.
abstract: NA: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm2. With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

title: The AI debate is missing half the system.
abstract: NA: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human-AI system, not the AI model alone.

title: My hidden homeless past.

Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity.
abstract: NA: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet.
abstract: NA: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS3), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κaa) and the transverse (κab) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet.
abstract: NA: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria.
abstract: NA: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

title: Human interferon-α autoantibody development broadens reactivity and enables functional synergy.
abstract: NA: Neutralizing autoantibodies against interferon-α (IFN-α) are associated with severe viral infections but may improve outcomes in IFN-α-driven autoimmunity. How these antibodies emerge, mature, and function at the molecular level remains unclear. Here, we tracked development of plasma neutralizing activity against all 12 IFN-αs in multiple human donors over years. Plasma neutralization frequently initiated with narrow IFN-α specificity, often against IFN-α8, but increased in breadth and potency with individual kinetics. Monoclonal antibody analyses revealed that affinity maturation generated epitope-specific antibody classes, highlighting parallel emergence of subtype-restricted and broadly reactive antibodies. Biophysical and structural characterization of human antibody-IFN-α complexes uncovered determinants of initial specificity and breadth development. Antibodies engaging non-competing, neutralizing epitopes acted co-operatively to block IFN-α signaling, and some combinations triggered Fc-effector functions via cell surface IFN-α:IFNAR2 interactions that may eliminate IFN-α-responsive cells. Our findings reveal features shaping anti-IFN-α autoantibody repertoires and synergistic mechanisms that amplify their potency and pathogenic potential.

title: Granzyme K is a driver of age-related tissue remodeling and functional decline independently of age-associated immune dysfunction.
abstract: NA: Aging is characterized by progressive tissue and organ decline, with chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) implicated as a central driver. Granzyme K (GzmK), a serine protease that is markedly upregulated in aged memory CD8+ T cells, is proposed to be a central mediator of both immune and organismal aging. Using young and aged GzmK-/- mice, we showed that GzmK was dispensable for the major hallmarks of immune aging, including T cell dysfunction, but was a critical driver of age-related tissue decline. Despite persistent immune aging phenotypes, GzmK deficiency markedly attenuated organ aging, effectively uncoupling immune and tissue aging. In the kidney, this was associated with reduced complement deposition, whereas in the liver, improved function and reduced fibrosis occurred independently of complement, coinciding instead with increased decorin and reduced pro-fibrotic TGF-β signaling. These findings identify GzmK as a tissue-specific driver of organismal aging but not immune aging or systemic inflammaging.

title: TIGIT and PD-L1 co-blockade promotes dendritic cell-dependent production of non-exhausted CD8+ T cells.
abstract: NA: Combination immunotherapy targeting the coinhibitory molecules TIGIT and PD-L1 promotes non-exhausted CD8+ T cell differentiation in cancer. Because anti-TIGIT efficacy requires Fc binding, we investigated the role of Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-expressing myeloid cells in the mechanism of action. Conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) were required for therapeutic efficacy. Transcriptional profiling of intratumoral myeloid cells revealed an FcγR+ cDC type-1 (cDC1)-like activation state characterized by elevated costimulatory ligands for CD28 (CD80/CD86) and CD226 (PVR) that was enriched in Fc-active anti-TIGIT combination-treated tumors. Therapy-expanded CD8+ T cells expressed CD28 and upregulated CD226 upon treatment. Mechanistically, CD28 signaling was a prerequisite for therapy-induced CD226 expression on T cells, and cDC-derived PVR promoted CD226-mediated non-exhausted T cell differentiation. Type I interferon (IFN-I), induced through FcγR engagement, maintained and amplified the FcγR+ cDC1-like state, and exogenous IFN-I rescued anti-tumor immunity upon Fc-inert anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 combination. Thus, Fc-active anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 therapy promotes a sequential costimulatory cascade centered on cDCs, amplified by IFN-I signaling.

title: Frankenstein protein assembled by mRNA trans-splicing promotes cytokine release.
abstract: NA: Trans-splicing of pre-mRNAs to produce alternate proteins is known to occur in unicellular and invertebrate organisms; yet whether such events occur and produce functional proteins in mammals remains unclear. In a recent issue of Nature, macrophages polarized to an inflammatory state were found to produce several chimeric RNAs through trans-splicing with consequences for the inflammatory response.

title: Phosphocreatine strengthens CD8+ T cells by remodeling chromatin.
abstract: NA: Metabolites can regulate T cell gene expression and effector function, but how changes in mitochondrial ATP production influence chromatin remodeling remains unclear. In a recent issue of Cell, Ng et al. demonstrate that D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) increases oxidative phosphorylation and phosphocreatine production, promoting chromatin accessibility and CD8+ T cell effector function to limit tumor growth.

title: Dendritic cells drive next-generation checkpoint blockade immunotherapy.
abstract: NA: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s) are key orchestrators of antitumor immunity. In this issue of Immunity, Luri-Rey et al. and Duong et al. show that two next-generation checkpoint strategies act through mature cDC1s, which assemble the costimulatory signals that set CD8⁺ T cell fate and determine therapeutic efficacy.

title: Allergic resident memory finds a skin niche.
abstract: NA: Mechanisms driving allergic relapse in the skin remain poorly defined. In this issue of Immunity, Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ subset of skin-resident memory CD4+ T cells that persist after biologic treatment in human atopic dermatitis.

title: The stromal pit crew keeps GCs racing with PD-L1.
abstract: NA: The PD-1/PD-L1 axis is a pivotal yet incompletely understood regulator of germinal center responses. In this issue of Immunity, Akama-Garren et al. demonstrate that PD-L1 expression on stromal cells enhances T-B cell collaborations and humoral immunity.

title: Egg-ception to the rule: Monocyte-derived microglia infiltrate CVOs.
abstract: NA: Circumventricular organs (CVOs) are specialized interfaces between the peripheral circulation and the brain. In this issue of Immunity, Van Hove et al. reveal CVOs as distinct immune niches that shape brain macrophage identity. These environments generate specialized macrophage phenotypes and enable fetal monocytes to adopt bona fide microglial identities, thereby demonstrating how local tissue context can influence immune cell fate.

title: Tumor-to-dendritic cell reprogramming induces immunogenic lymphoid structures across cancers.
abstract: NA: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors are associated with improved responses to immunotherapy. Here, we examined the impact of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s) in TLS formation. Reprogrammed tumor cells into cDC1-like cells remodeled the tumor microenvironment and induced immunogenic TLSs (imgTLSs) across melanoma, colon, bladder, breast, and pancreatic cancer models with distinct genetic backgrounds. cDC1-like cells activated lymphotoxin, TNF, and interferon programs and engaged early with T cells through MHC class I and CD40 signaling to induce imgTLSs containing BCL6+ germinal centers, independently of endogenous cDC1s. Intratumoral positioning shaped distinct cDC1-like cell states, with DC-LAMP+ CCR7+ migratory cDC1s nucleating niches enriched in CD4+, CD8+ T cells, and B cells in mouse and human tumors. ImgTLSs sustained B and T cell responses and promoted systemic immunity through expansion of shared clonotypes in distant, untreated tumors. Our findings outline the spatial organization, signaling programs and interactions of cDC1-like cells that initiate intratumoral lymphoid structures and establish cellular reprogramming as a strategy toward overcoming resistance to immunotherapy.

title: Mitochondrial DNA abundance is a determinant of immunogenic cell death in cancer.
abstract: NA: Cells experiencing mitochondrial stress can undergo apoptosis or cell death that triggers innate immune activation. We examined the mechanisms determining these distinct outcomes in cancer. Abundant mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and high expression of the cGAS-STING pathway were features of KRAS-mutant cancers. In a pharmacological screen, MEK inhibitor (MEKi) effectively induced mtDNA release into the cytosol in KRAS-mutant cancer cells. However, MEKi also induced PRKN-mediated mitophagy, which limited mtDNA release by eliminating damaged mitochondria. Inhibition of mitophagy sustained mtDNA efflux and amplified cGAS-STING signaling. Mechanistically, PRKN-mediated mitophagy restrained mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) to limit mtDNA efflux. The balance between mtDNA and cytochrome c (cyt.c) release defined two immunologically distinct outcomes: immunogenic cell death (ICD) and apoptosis. In preclinical models, combined inhibition of MEK and mitophagy induced robust dendritic cell (DC) activation and promoted CD8+ T cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Consistently, PRKN expression negatively correlated with immune infiltration in human cancers. Collectively, these findings provide a rationale for combination strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics to augment antitumor immunity.

title: Growth factor VEGF-B sustains intestinal Tfh cell stemness to restrict Taurinivorans outgrowth and microbiota-driven obesity.
abstract: NA: Autocrine signaling through vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 (VEGFR-1) reprograms T cell metabolism upon TCR stimulation. We found that mice bearing conditional deletion of Flt1 (encoding VEGFR-1) in T cells developed spontaneous obesity with advancing age. Analyses of lymphoid and metabolic tissues identified a VEGFR-1+ T follicular helper (Tfh) population in Peyer's patches and mesenteric lymph nodes. Flt1 deletion impaired Tfh fitness and reduced secretory IgA in the gut, resulting in unrestricted expansion of the pathobiont Taurinivorans. Taurinivorans overgrowth depleted host taurine, which drove obesity via suppressed adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis. Mechanistically, a VEGFR-1-AKT signaling axis promoted Tfh cell stemness by limiting p53-mediated senescence. This Tfh-microbiota-obesity pathway was also observed in diet-induced obese mice and in humans. Oral administration of IgA reduced Taurinivorans and alleviated adiposity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of this axis. Tfh cell senescence impairs IgA production, disrupting gut microbial homeostasis, with consequences to host metabolic disease.

title: T cell cross-priming by PD-L1+ type 1 conventional dendritic cells mediates the antitumor efficacy of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody.
abstract: NA: Bispecific antibodies that conditionally engage costimulatory receptors aim to enhance antitumor T cell immunity while limiting systemic toxicity. We investigated mechanisms underlying the clinical performance of a PD-L1×4-1BB bispecific antibody. Therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1×4-1BB was largely independent of PD-L1 expression on malignant cells but waned in Batf3-/- mice or upon depletion of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1-specific deletion of PD-L1 markedly limited tumor control. PD-L1×4-1BB enhanced proliferation of tumor-antigen-specific CD8+ T cells through mechanisms dependent on cross-presentation, the presence of interleukin (IL)-12, 4-1BB costimulation, and CD40L-mediated cDC1 licensing. PD-L1×4-1BB increased cDC1-T cell contacts, which promoted transcriptional programs associated with T cell activation and proliferation. Treated tumors exhibited increased infiltration and spatial proximity of cDC1s and activated CD8+ T cells. Accordingly, increasing dendritic-cell abundance via Flt3L further enhanced tumor control. Thus, cDC1-T cell interactions are central to PD-L1×4-1BB activity, with antigen cross-presentation, dendritic-cell licensing, and IL-12 and 4-1BB costimulation converging to promote antitumor immunity.

title: PD-L1 expression in germinal centers promotes humoral immunity by restricting T follicular regulatory cell differentiation.
abstract: NA: Germinal center (GC) responses generate humoral immunity through coordinated interactions between B cells and T follicular helper (TFH) and T follicular regulatory (TFR) cells. Despite high expression of PD-1 by TFH and TFR cells, the function of its ligand PD-L1 in the GC is unclear. Here, we show an immunogenic role for PD-L1 via tuning T-B collaboration to promote humoral immunity. Integrated analyses of secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) revealed that B cell zone reticular cells (BRCs), including follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), expressed PD-L1. BRC expression of PD-L1 facilitated GC formation and enabled loss of B cell tolerance in autoantibody disease. Mechanistically, BRC-specific deletion of PD-L1 enhanced TFH cell production of Sostdc1 and TFR cell differentiation, destabilizing T-B contacts in the GC. Patient-derived tumor biopsies indicated that a tumor-infiltrating TFH SOSTDC1 signature inversely correlated with immunotherapy responsiveness. These findings reveal a non-canonical immunogenic role for PD-L1 in the GC and suggest that augmenting B cell responses could improve the efficacy of PD-L1 blockade.

title: A microbiome-reactive TMIGD2hi Th17 subset is spatially enriched at the intestinal epithelium and expanded in inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: NA: Subsets of intestinal CD4+ T cells directly recognize commensal bacteria and coordinate tolerance versus protective immunity. Our limited understanding of CD4+ T cell specificities and corresponding functional phenotypes has created a barrier to deciphering the mechanisms of mucosal homeostasis and inflammation mediated by the adaptive immune system. To address this, we leveraged an immunodominant Bacteroidetes epitope in SusC to perform single-cell profiling of the SusC-specific and total CD4+ T cell landscapes in intestinal tissues of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). By analyzing phenotypes and T cell receptor specificities in parallel, we uncovered phenotypic diversification of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in IBD and identified an epithelial-localized, SusC-reactive Th17 subset that is BACH2lo, GZMAhi, and expresses the costimulatory receptor TMIGD2. Together, our results highlight the utility of tracking commensal-specific T cell responses to define specialized subsets of Th17 cells associated with loss of tolerance to the microbiome.

title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond.
abstract: NA: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

title: NF-κB phosphorylation controls enhancer selection to shape the inflammatory gene program.
abstract: NA: Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. Genes linked to these enhancers, including inflammatory mediators, were selectively impaired in S276A macrophages. Although antiviral responses remained intact, Rela Ser276Ala mice resisted endotoxin shock but were susceptible to bacterial infection. Thus, NF-κB responses are functionally partitioned by enhancer architecture: phosphorylation-sensitive sites define a latent enhancer compartment with NF-κB-dominated regulatory architecture, whereas primed sites are embedded in broader networks of lineage-determining and inducible TFs, yielding distinct biological outputs.

title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation.
abstract: NA: Macrophages are among the most versatile differentiated cell types in the body, serving as key regulators of tissue development, homeostasis, inflammation, repair, and immunity. Their functional diversity cannot be captured by fixed subsets, binary activation states, or single-marker definitions. Macrophage identity emerges instead from the integration of developmental origin, tissue niche, epigenetic history, local environmental cues, and disease-associated signals. Advances in single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, epigenomics, in vivo perturbation, and computational modeling now show that this behavior is organized through modular gene programs, so that any given macrophage state is best described as a weighted combination of program activities rather than a discrete label. We argue that embracing this modular architecture matters not only for annotation but for therapy: macrophage-directed interventions will require defining disease-associated states, identifying surface-accessible entry points into them, and rewiring the underlying programs with spatial and temporal precision.

title: Viscoelastic Niches Shape γδ T Cell Phenotype and Effector Function.
abstract: NA: γδ T-cells, which are enriched in epithelial tissues, have been used in cancer therapy because of their capacity for rapid, MHC-independent cytotoxicity. However, current paradigms largely overlook the role of tissue mechanical cues in regulating γδ T-cell function. Here, we investigated how matrix viscoelasticity modulates γδ T-cell migration, differentiation state, phenotype, and function, using a tunable collagen-based gel system. Slow-relaxing matrices preserved a less differentiated phenotype, reduced migration, and increased FAS and PD-1 expression. Despite increased PD-1 expression, these cells remained functional, demonstrated by high levels of TNF-α and IFN-γ relative to PD-1-negative cells. Proteomic analysis revealed that γδ T-cells respond to changes in viscoelasticity through actin remodeling and shifts in metabolic machinery. Functionally, cells encapsulated in slow-relaxing gels showed improved control of tumor growth in an aggressive HCT116 tumor model. Together, these findings establish matrix viscoelasticity as an important regulator of post-thymic γδ T-cell differentiation and function.

title: miRNA delivery via nanowires restores functional responses in aged T cells.
abstract: NA: Aging reshapes CD8+ T cell immunity by depleting naive populations, narrowing repertoire diversity, and promoting dysfunctional states, thereby weakening responses to infection or vaccination. This study presents a polyethyleneimine (PEI)-functionalized silicon nanowire platform for high-viability, non-viral delivery of single or multiplexed microRNAs (miRNAs) into resting aged CD8+ T cells. Nanowires enable transient modulation of transcriptional programs governing T cell activation, metabolism, proliferation, and differentiation. Delivering a single miRNA influences early activation and differentiation stages, while multiplexed miRNA delivery leads to a broader boost in activation responses, effector functions, metabolic health, and cell proliferation. In vivo, ex vivo-treated aged CD8+ T cells exhibit enhanced early effector priming following antigen exposure. Similarly, in aged human CD8+ T cells, multiplexed miRNA enhances activation and cytotoxic responses and sustains an effector-primed state during early activation and expansion. This method consistently improves function across donors aged from healthy individuals to those with current or past cancer.

title: A 4D Bio-Kirigami Strategy for Engineering Complex Tissue Curvatures.
abstract: NA: Native tissues exhibit intricate curvatures essential for their function yet recapitulating structural complexity and dynamic morphogenesis remains challenging. Here, we present a cytocompatible bio-Kirigami system that enables programmable transformation of cell-laden hydrogels into complex three-dimensional tissue constructs. The system consists of (1) a photocrosslinked hydrogel with tunable degradation and swelling behavior to drive shape transformation and (2) a rigid hydrogel frame to provide structural support. Spatial patterning encodes localized swelling differentials via sequential photolithography, enabling controlled deformation and diverse morphing behaviors. Stem cell-laden bio-Kirigami constructs underwent programmed shape transformation and developed into tissue-like structures with complex curvatures under tissue-specific culture conditions. Importantly, the engineered tissue constructs retained their structural integrity and shape after removal of the supporting frame. This bio-Kirigami strategy provides a versatile approach for engineering dynamically transformable tissue constructs that recapitulate the complex geometries of native tissues.

title: A long-acting injectable nanoparticle-hydrogel depot enables sustained IGF-1 delivery to reverse chronic denervation.
abstract: NA: Chronic denervation following peripheral nerve injury leads to progressive muscle atrophy and Schwann cell dysfunction that severely limit functional recovery, yet no therapies effectively sustain trophic support over the prolonged regenerative period. Here, we develop a long-acting injectable (LAI) biomaterial platform that enables sustained local delivery of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1). The system encapsulates IGF-1 in poly(ethylene glycol)-b-polycaprolactone nanoparticles and embeds nanoparticles within an injectable nanofiber-hydrogel composite, enabling six-week local IGF-1 delivery with preserved bioactivity and tissue retention. In a rat chronic denervation model with delayed nerve repair, the IGF-1 LAI increased grip strength by 29.1%, myelinated axon counts by 186.2%, and myofiber cross-sectional area by 88.4%. In a non-human primate model, repeated six-week dosing maintained intramuscular IGF-1 levels and improved functional recovery by 57.0%, accompanied by reduced fibrosis and increased reinnervation. These findings establish a translational biomaterial strategy for sustained protein delivery and disease-modifying treatment of chronic denervation.

title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis.
abstract: NA: The design of atomically precise catalysts requires strategies that regulate their electronic and structural dynamics under operating conditions. While conventional doping can effectively tune bulk materials, it translates poorly to single-atom catalysts (SACs), in which isolated atoms lack extended coordination and are prone to oxidative instability. Here we design atomically dispersed Ru-O-Cr motifs that enable oxidation damping during acidic oxygen evolution. In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy shows attenuated Ru oxidation synchronized with anticorrelated and partially reversible Cr redox evolution, consistent with proximity-dependent redox coupling. This buffered redox response is accompanied by bounded and partially reversible changes in the local metal-oxygen coordination environment. These coupled dynamics support proximity-coupled Ru-O-Cr redox units, enabling a 55.7-fold increased resistance against oxidation-induced Ru dissolution compared with conventional SACs. In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis, catalysts incorporating proximal Ru-O-Cr configurations exhibit degradation rates that are 6.8-fold and 14.4-fold lower than those of Ru SACs and commercial RuO2, respectively, at 1 A cm-2. These results suggest proximal oxidation damping as a potential design principle for stabilizing atomically precise electrocatalysts.

title: Nonlinear waveguide polaritons for long-distance propagation of spins at room temperature.
Soft polymer coatings form hard directional bonding.
Spin order steers a light-matter condensate.
Imaging multi-particle dynamics in space and time.
Nanoparticles as carrier and drug.
In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites.
abstract: NA: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) and the resulting malignant tumour ascites characterize advanced gastrointestinal cancers, often leading to poor prognosis and limited response to current therapies. Single-cell analysis of patient-derived PM and malignant tumour ascites reveals an approximately 90% enrichment of TREM2+-tumour-associated macrophages, which drive CD8+ T cell dysfunction and tumour growth. Here we develop lipid nanoparticles encapsulating mRNA to reprogram these tumour-associated macrophages into chimeric antigen receptor macrophages targeting Claudin18.2-positive tumour ascites. The lipid nanoparticles incorporate a TREM2+ ligand to enhance the targeting of TREM2 macrophages. The piperazine-containing phosphoramide ionizable lipid synergizes with the TREM2 ligand to inhibit ligand dissociation, promoting TREM2 internalization and degradation via lysosomal and autophagosomal pathways. This inhibits AKT signalling and reprograms tumour-associated macrophages towards an antitumour phenotype, enhancing progenitor exhausted and effector memory CD8+ T cell responses, altering the PM transcriptome, and reducing immunosuppression in both malignant tumour ascites and tumours. Combined with PD-1 blockade, this therapy suppresses tumour growth and extends survival in mice, and with matching immunological effects in clinical samples, demonstrates its translational potential for PM immunotherapy.

title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors.
abstract: NA: Spatiotemporal optical microscopies are powerful tools to image the propagation of energy carriers in materials, including electrons, excitons, magnons and polaritons, providing key functional metrics inaccessible to contact-based transport measurements. Nevertheless, these approaches do not distinguish single-particle from multi-particle quantum states, hindering the study of many-body correlations that underlie the complex phase diagrams at the heart of contemporary materials research. Here we extend a concept derived from multidimensional spectroscopy, called intensity cycling, to the spatiotemporal domain using transient scattering microscopy. We leverage this approach to selectively image single-particle and multi-particle transport in van der Waals semiconductors. We demonstrate a series of sought-after capabilities, including clean isolation of single-particle charge transport with high signal-to-noise ratio, spatiotemporal tracking of exciton-exciton annihilation, high-throughput mapping of dielectric disorder, and imaging the emergence of a polaronic Mott transition and correlated transport in a superatomic solid. This work delivers a precision tool capable of visualizing how many-body interactions shape material function.

title: Model systems and integration strategies to capture human biology.
abstract: NA: Modelling human biology is difficult precisely because many of the responses that matter most emerge not within a single tissue or cell type, but at the boundaries where matrix, immune and systemic signals converge in ways that are hard to recreate in isolation. Conventional in vitro systems and animal studies have advanced our understanding of many physiological processes, but they still consistently fall short at these interfaces. In this Review, we discuss how engineered materials, organoids, microphysiological systems and computational models can be used together to build more informative human model systems. We first consider engineered materials as tools for controlling the local environment around cells, including matrix composition, stiffness, geometry, transport and time-dependent cues. We then examine organoids, assembloids and microphysiological system platforms, with emphasis on functional benchmarking, vascularization, immune integration, maturation, reproducibility and biological variation across donors and conditions. Finally, we discuss computational models, including spatial atlases, generative models and digital twins, as tools for organizing measurements, testing mechanisms and improving prediction. A key insight is that no current platform fully closes the loop between sensing, tissue modelling, computational calibration and feedback-guided intervention. The central challenge now is to build models whose complexity is justified by the human question they are designed to answer.

title: Mechanical adaptation drives out-of-equilibrium network reorganization and self-strengthening in adapt-ring networks.
abstract: NA: Synthetic polymer networks typically lack the ability to autonomously remodel and strengthen under mechanical stress, a capability commonly observed in natural materials. Here we introduce adapt-ring networks (ARNs) that establish a general design principle for adaptive polymer materials. ARNs couple a covalent polyethylene glycol network with reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains whose strain-directed fragmentation, translocation and alignment form kinetically trapped architectures encoding local mechanical history. Mechanical training enhances Young's modulus, tensile strength, fracture energy and fatigue threshold by up to an order of magnitude, with full reversibility through solvent-induced crystalline-domain reformation. Spatially resolved adaptation and 3D printability enable gradient materials and customized architectures. Incorporating polyethylene glycol side chains to form dangling-chain ARNs enables strain-controlled out-of-equilibrium growth through threading and crystallization of external α-cyclodextrins. These hydrogels autonomously generate spatially self-organized, strain-dependent reinforcement, including non-local, environment-fed stiffening conceptually analogous to biological reinforcement. These features establish a general approach to bio-inspired, non-equilibrium soft materials that adapt, remember, regrow and readapt.

title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency.
abstract: NA: Nanoparticle superlattices enable programmable material structure through ligand-mediated interactions, but attractive ligand interactions typically limit assembly to densely packed lattices that maximize nearest-neighbour bonding. Intentionally programmed directional bonding and valency are therefore typically assumed to require particle-level anisotropy in shape or surface patterning. Here, using assemblies of flexible, electrostatically active isotropic nanoparticles, we show that valency need not be encoded by particle geometry, but can instead emerge spontaneously during assembly. When ligand coronas are sufficiently deformable, ligands reconfigure to align along interparticle interfaces, generating an effective valency. Using a combination of experiment and simulation, we show that increasing ligand deformability lowers lattice coordination numbers, and identify design considerations for assembling isotropic building blocks into lattices with lower coordination, packing density and symmetry than would be predicted from hard-sphere packing. The work presented here therefore establishes ligand flexibility as a design parameter for programming coordination in nanoparticle assembly.

title: Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons.
abstract: NA: The optical spin Hall effect enables the spatial separation of four domains of circularly polarized light from a linearly polarized source through photonic spin-orbit coupling, which arises from non-degenerate transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic modes. This mechanism is ineffective for incoherent photoluminescence. In transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers, bright excitons possess in-plane electric dipoles and strong oscillator strengths, whereas dark excitons have out-of-plane dipoles. Here, by embedding WS2 monolayers in waveguide microcavities, we demonstrate strong coupling between bright excitons and photonic modes, forming exciton-polaritons. Under non-resonant pumping, dark excitons become strongly populated and feed both transverse-magnetic- and transverse-electric-like exciton-polariton modes, each with an out-of-plane electric-field component. We observe the optical spin Hall effect in waveguide polaritons, leading to the formation of eight polarization domains and spin-polarized polariton currents propagating up to 92 ± 1 μm at room temperature. These results establish transition metal dichalcogenide-based polaritonic waveguides as a promising platform for room-temperature spin-optoelectronic devices.

title: Process-intrinsic cellular network for sustained strength-ductility across temperatures in a 3D-printed multi-principal-element alloy.
abstract: NA: Laser-based additive manufacturing (LAM) provides a transformative route for fabricating Cr-Fe-Co-Ni-Al-Ti-based multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs). These alloys typically rely on L12 precipitate strengthening and thus require post-processing; however, such treatments rarely ensure stable mechanical performance over a wide temperature range. Here we designed a (CrFeCo)48Ni34Al7Ti5V5Ta1 MPEA with a self-assembled body-centred cubic/L21 precipitate cellular network formed intrinsically during LAM. Slip transfer and back-stress hardening across Kurdjumov-Sachs and Nishiyama-Wassermann interfaces and a weakly temperature-dependent stacking fault energy stabilize the dislocation-mediated deformation from 77 to 873 K. Consequently, the MPEA maintains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range, indicating relatively stable tensile performance. This process-intrinsic pathway circumvents the need for post-treatment and reveals interface-mediated plasticity mechanisms. Our findings demonstrate that interface coherency engineering provides a foundation for designing strong yet ductile alloys with reduced temperature sensitivity via LAM.

title: Writing monolayer oxides with electrons.
Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces.
abstract: NA: Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light-matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS2) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton-polaritons, rendering ReS2 a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS2 into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS2, these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton-polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit.
abstract: NA: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX-MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3.
abstract: NA: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, non-volatile memory and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films in which polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, whereas off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO3 with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics.

title: Metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors.
Engineering therapeutic delivery.
Lipid nanoparticles call the shots as mRNA medicine takes off.
III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects.
abstract: NA: In-sensor computing enables real-time and intelligent analysis with superior energy efficiency. However, existing oxide-based or 2D-ferroelectric-based in-sensor computing devices suffer from severe response loss and challenges in large-scale fabrication. Here a III-nitride-based in-sensing computing device is proposed by exploiting its intrinsic polarization effects in their heterostructures. The polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers and the defect-free nature of bipolar polarization interfaces effectively avoid carrier recombination losses, enabling high light sensitivity level of nanowatt per square centimetre, responsivity level of 106 A W-1 and on/off ratio level of 105 in the sensor-memristor mode. Additionally, controlled applied bias allows the sensor-memristor to transform into a high-speed detector. These results establish a viable design principle that utilizes interfacial-electrostatics-induced photocarrier spatial separation and asymmetric-barriers-modulated carrier transport to realize in-sensor computing. Moreover, the high-temperature resistance of III-nitrides allows the device to maintain high performance at temperatures up to 300 °C. This approach aligns with industrial-scale III-nitride manufacturing and complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor integration, probably advancing the feasibility of in-sensor computing architectures.

title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels.
abstract: NA: Nanofluidic memristors promise brain-inspired information processing with ions, yet their microscopic origin remains debated. So far, ionic memory has been attributed to ion-specific interactions, dynamic wetting, chemical reactions or mechanical deformations, yet typically without direct experimental evidence. Here, by combining operando interferometric imaging with electrokinetic measurements, we directly visualize voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of two-dimensional (2D) nanochannels as the key origin of memristive hysteresis. We identify two distinct classes of blisters: unidirectional, driven by electrostatic forces on surface charges, and bidirectional, arising from osmotic pressure due to concentration polarization. This mechanistic framework explains device evolution and device-to-device variability, and reframes stochastic blistering as a functional design element. Our results constitute a direct proof of electromechanical coupling as a robust pathway to ionic memory in 2D nanochannels and open routes towards high-performance ionic memristors and electrically actuated nanofluidic valves.

title: Strain turns carbon dioxide into circular polyesters.
Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory.
abstract: NA: Magnonic circuits that use spin waves for nanoscale signal processing and computing are widely regarded as a promising alternative to traditional semiconductor electronics. However, a key missing component of this information nanotechnology is a feasible approach for the integration of memory directly into spin-wave devices. Here we propose a strategy for the implementation of built-in non-volatile memory, which uses the static magnetization states of waveguiding elements within a magnonic network fabricated from a low-loss magnetic insulator and operating at zero bias magnetic field. We show that switching the magnetization direction in these elements enables efficient control over spin-wave propagation paths. Furthermore, we suggest an approach to achieve low-energy selective magnetization switching in such systems. Our results open new possibilities for the realization of advanced, self-contained magnonic nano-circuits.

title: Genes take control of active matter.
Bridging microwaves and light.
Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring.
abstract: NA: Metal-free molecular magnets differ from conventional magnetic devices that predominantly rely on metallic magnets as these metal-free materials may offer biocompatibility and bioresorbability. However, existing molecular materials lack the ferromagnetic strength required for high-fidelity sensing at clinically relevant tissue depths. Here we introduce a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet derived from graphitic carbon nitride, combining metallic-level ferromagnetism with full bioresorbability. De-nitrogenation creates spin centres coupled through a reconstructed π-σ conjugated framework, conferring robust spontaneous magnetization that remains stable under physiological conditions. Integrated with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and silk fibroin, the material forms catheter-deliverable epicardial patches for cardiac tracking and can also be dispersed in injectable hydrogels for organ-scale sensing, including the three-dimensional reconstruction of localized hepatic pathologies. Coupled with a skin-interfaced Hall array, this magnetic sensing architecture provides the continuous, untethered monitoring of multi-organ dynamics, robust against motion artifacts and tissue impedance. In porcine models, it facilitates the continuous assessment of ejection fraction over 4 weeks, followed by benign bioresorption. Benchmarked against standard-of-care echocardiography, this approach delivers clinical-grade trajectories, supporting longitudinal, infrastructure-independent physiological monitoring.

title: A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research.
A comprehensive analysis of CBER experience with AAV gene therapy IND submissions.
Biotechnologies for climate resilience.
Low-methane rice is near - the world should deploy it.
Silence snapped up for $1.3 billion.
The world's two loves.
Are AI tech giants hijacking drug discovery?
A new era for Parkinson's: this time with better stem cells.
Biotech news from around the world.
UK Biobank adds immune and brain health layers.
China plans ban on biotech exports.
How biotechnology can mitigate climate change by curbing the global land squeeze.
Searching perturbation dictionaries with RNA fingerprints.
Dual-layer engineering of herbicide resistance in crops.
De novo design of proteases.
Deployability of biotechnologies for environmentally resilient agriculture.
abstract: NA: Agriculture is both humanity's largest infrastructure and the leading driver of environmental degradation. Many early-stage biotechnologies could mitigate this impact, but their deployability has not been systematically evaluated. We analyze deployability of 77 biotechnologies across eight domains (crops, soils, livestock, watersheds, aquaculture, health and security, food loss/waste and frontiers) by applying a Balanced Readiness Level assessment spanning technological, market, regulatory, acceptance and organizational dimensions. We find that market viability and social acceptance, not technological readiness, represent the primary constraints. High-readiness technologies tend to be 'drop-in', contained, transient and perceived as natural. These characteristics indicate strategies to elevate overall deployability, such as addressing genetically modified organism containment.
