Assessing the scalability and environmental impacts of biotechnologies for prioritization requires additional quantitative analysis, as shown in a Fermi analysis of microbial fertilizers. We combine our findings into a near- to long-term roadmap for living infrastructure: predictively designed multicomponent biological communities that function as systems at the ecosystem level to enhance food security and environmental resilience.

title: Lasting genetic control of mosquito-borne diseases is within reach.
Cellular agriculture for sustainable and programmable foods.
abstract: NA: Cellular agriculture promises to reduce the environmental burden and inefficiencies of food systems. The question is no longer whether precision fermentation and cultivated meat production can produce alternative proteins and other food components, but whether they can attain the cost, scale and quality required for broad adoption. We examine cellular agriculture through the interrelated lenses of enabling technologies, food function and manufacturing economics. The field is approaching an inflection point where biological technology development is less important for commercial success than achieving scalable, affordable manufacturing. Key challenges include how products and their functional attributes are designed and how production processes are configured. For precision fermentation, the most compelling opportunities lie in functional approaches to improve taste, nutritional quality, health benefits and formulation rather than in direct imitation of existing foods or ingredients. For cultivated meat production, impact will come first from hybrid and ingredient-based products that capture specific values of cellular ingredients while avoiding the costs of full tissue mimicry.

title: Microbes should make what petroleum can't.
The next frontier in nitrogen fixation.
Three questions with climate biotech startup founders.
The seeds of resilience.
Scientific team structures behind FDA-approved drugs.
Climate biotechnology.
Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response.
abstract: NA: To elucidate the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response (DDR) network, we conduct unbiased genetic interaction screens using Cas12a. We disrupt 233 DDR genes frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, either individually or in pairwise combinations, enabling us to assess the phenotypic effects induced by the loss of DDR gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth conditions. We identify high-confidence positive and negative gene-gene interactions, along with connections between previously unlinked DDR pathways. Among the identified genetic interactions, we uncover synthetic lethal interactions between genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1-Pol ζ complex and the MCM8-MCM9-HROB DNA helicase complex, between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes, as well as between genes encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex, suggesting opportunities for targeted treatments in tumors carrying mutations in these genes. Collectively, our genetic map of the DDR network identifies synthetic lethal and buffering interactions with therapeutic potential.

title: Editor's Pick: Wild Bioscience.
An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
abstract: NA: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo.
abstract: NA: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform's high-order multiplexing.

title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table.
Recordanelles capture transient gene expression in single human cells.
Human Argonaute 2 is a programmable targeting domain for RNA editing.
Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
abstract: NA: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.
abstract: NA: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity.
abstract: NA: Microorganisms have the potential to deliver growth-promoting benefits to plants and crops; however, to be useful in a field setting, their gene expression should be programmable and restricted to specific plant hosts and conditions. Here, using O-methyl-L-tyrosine (OMY) as a model compound, we establish noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a tool for plant-based control of associated microbial activity. We use genetic code expansion to engineer OMY-dependent control of protein synthesis in the soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis. Engineered B. subtilis strains express an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pair that, upon provision of OMY, results in suppression of in-frame amber stop codons in target transcripts. We engineer Arabidopsis, tomato and poplar to biosynthesize OMY, showing that plant-derived OMY can stimulate gene expression in both model and wild soil bacteria. This demonstrates that inducible and tissue-specific expression of a single biosynthetic enzyme by the plant enables on-demand control over microbial activity, establishing ncAAs as a tool for programming plant-microorganism partnerships.

title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing.
abstract: NA: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.

title: Editor's pick: Bioptimus.
Designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine for enhanced solid tumour penetration and therapy.
abstract: NA: While nanomedicines hold great promise for solid tumour therapy, their penetration and access to tumour cells is limited by large glycosylated proteins called mucins that are enriched in the tumour microenvironment. Here we show that mucins induce the disassembly of self-assembled mPEG-polyester micellar nanoparticles into smaller unimers. Leveraging this finding, we designed a mucin-responsive, paclitaxel-conjugated nanomedicine (mrPNM) whose unimers are capable of escaping the mucin-binding barrier. Following intravenous injection, this designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine exhibited markedly deeper penetration than the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and albumin, resulting in 3.9- and 1.5-fold increases in tumour cell delivery, respectively, in a pancreatic mouse tumour model. The mrPNMs also achieved superior tumour growth inhibition compared to both the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and Abraxane, the FDA-approved nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel, in three solid tumour models. The mucin-responsive nanomedicine platform could provide a general strategy for improving the treatment of solid tumours.

title: Self-powered bubble motor microswarms for ultrasensitive detection, monitoring and prediction in cancer liquid biopsies.
abstract: NA: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have shown great potential for disease detection from liquid biopsies. However, the lack of optimized isolation and detection methods limited their clinical application. Here we engineer a bioinspired, reconfigurable, self-powered bubble motor (Butor) microswarm to streamline intelligent isolation and ultrasensitive profiling of circulating EVs for cancer liquid biopsies. Butor microswarm shows jellyfish-like, self-propelled lifting locomotion along lumen-like vertical or inclined tubular path in parallel, allowing rapid isolation (10 min, near 90%) of EV subtypes via three-dimensional directional scanning capture even in high-viscosity biofluids. Furthermore, the buoyancy-activated Butors achieve ultrasensitive EV profiling near a single-particle level, enable early diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer with an accuracy of up to 94% (95% sensitivity) in a pilot cohort and improve the outcome in cancer staging (I-IV) discrimination, response monitoring of surgical treatment and efficacy prediction of immunotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Our self-powered motor represents an intelligent, fast, inexpensive, sensitive and multiplexed liquid biopsy tool for accurate cancer diagnostics and treatment monitoring in clinical settings.

title: Author Correction: The malate shuttle detoxifies ammonia in exhausted T cells by producing 2-ketoglutarate.
Herpesvirus exposures map to self-reactivity networks in chronic disease.
Large-scale antibody reactome profiling identifies herpesvirus-autoantigen associations that underlie chronic diseases.
abstract: NA: Herpesviruses infect nearly all humans and have long been implicated in autoimmune and chronic diseases, yet their interactions with host proteins have not been systematically characterized. We profiled immunoglobulin G reactivities to >4,600 herpesvirus peptides and >15,000 human proteins using multiplexed protein display in two Mass General Brigham Biobank cohorts (discovery n = 1,289; replication n = 763), with longitudinal electronic health record follow-up. We identified and replicated 4,943 FDR-significant associations across 106 autoantigens, including previously uncharacterized viral-autoantigen axes, such as PHLDA1 and ZNF550. Eleven autoantigens were predicted by viral reactivities with >85% accuracy in independent validation, two of which exhibited viral-host sequence homology consistent with possible molecular mimicry. Integrating immune reactivities with incident diseases revealed virus-specific networks. Cytomegalovirus formed the largest multimorbid network, Epstein-Barr virus converged on pleiotropic autoimmune hubs and herpes simplex viruses formed partially overlapping networks. These findings define a herpesvirus-autoantigen-disease network atlas and prioritize candidate viral-host immune axes for mechanistic investigation.

title: Fever-induced OR560 promotes antibacterial immunity through macrophage pseudopod formation and phagocytosis.
abstract: NA: Fever is a conserved physiological response to pathogen infection. However, how fever promotes host defense remains poorly understood. Here we find that fever empowers antibacterial immunity by inducing olfactory receptor 560 (OR560) to promote macrophage phagocytosis. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we discovered that OR560 is indispensable for macrophage phagocytosis. Febrile temperature drives the serum response factor-dependent OR560 induction in macrophages to boost phagocytosis. OR560 responds to bacteria-derived peptides and plays an essential role in mediating pseudopod formation-a key step required for target uptake. Modulation of body temperature in mice showed that the immune-amplifying effect of fever depends predominantly on OR560. We further demonstrated that the genetic ablation of either Olfr560 or serum response factor (Srf) in mice not only abolished fever-potentiated macrophage phagocytosis but also led to catastrophic defects in bacterial clearance and increased mortality upon infections. Thus, our work reveals that OR560 is a pivotal regulator of fever-enhanced antibacterial phagocytosis and integrates both pathogen-derived and febrile signals to ensure a robust response to infection.

title: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4+ T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
abstract: NA: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

title: Early-life obesity edits T cell fate.
An ultrasound-triggered nanoplatform for enhanced sonodynamic immunotherapy achieved through Diels-Alder bond cleavage and in situ vaccine formation.
abstract: NA: Sonodynamic immunotherapy (SIT) presents prominent potential in amplified therapy against malignant tumors due to its precise spatiotemporal controllability and systemic immune activation capability. However, achieving synergistic integration of sonodynamic therapy (SDT) and immunotherapy to maximize anti-tumor efficacy remains an urgent and critical challenge. Herein, we constructed an ultrasound-triggered nanoplatform (MRPT), where MRPT could generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) for SDT under ultrasound irradiation, while the Diels-Alder (D-A) bond was broken to release immunoadjuvant R837 and capture tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) as in-situ vaccine for enhanced SIT. The exposed Mal groups enabled efficient binding to sulfhydryl groups of TAAs, facilitating efficient antigen capture, where the amount of ovalbumin captured by MRPT was around 2.7-fold that without ultrasound. Benefiting from SDT-induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), R837-mediated immune-stimulation, as well as in-situ vaccine formed by captured TAAs, the proportion of mature dendritic cells (DCs) in the spleen significantly increased up to 40.6%, CD8+ T cell infiltration was promoted, and regulatory T cell (Treg) proportion was also greatly reduced. Thus, this strategy offers a promising avenue for enhanced SIT in malignant tumor treatment. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Sonodynamic immunotherapy offers a promising strategy for treating malignant tumors, yet its therapeutic efficacy is often limited by the insufficient coordination between sonodynamic therapy and immune activation. In this study, we developed an ultrasound-triggered MRPT nanoplatform that integrates reactive oxygen species generation, immunoadjuvant release, and tumor-associated antigen capture within a single system. Upon ultrasound irradiation, MRPT efficiently induced immunogenic cell death, released the immune agonist R837, and exposed maleimide groups for enhanced capture of tumor-associated antigens, with an approximately 2.7-fold increase in ovalbumin capture compared with the non-irradiated condition. This multifunctional design promoted dendritic-cell maturation, enhanced CD8+ T-cell infiltration, and reduced regulatory T-cell proportions, thereby remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that ultrasound-regulated antigen capture and immune stimulation can effectively strengthen sonodynamic immunotherapy and provide a promising platform for developing more potent tumor vaccines and systemic antitumor immune responses.

title: Early-Life Farm Exposure and Food Allergy.
abstract: NA: Food allergy has increased substantially, increasing interest in environmental exposures that may promote immune tolerance. The "farm effect," in which children raised in traditional farming environments have lower rates of allergic disease, may also extend to food allergy. This review summarizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking prenatal and early-life farm exposures with food allergy and related atopic outcomes. Protective associations likely reflect combined exposures to livestock, farm dust, environmental microbes, diet, and farm milk during critical developmental windows. Proposed mechanisms include altered gut microbiome maturation, microbial metabolites, reduced epithelial inflammation, innate immune programming, and enhanced regulatory T-cell responses. However, direct evidence for clinically confirmed food allergy remains limited compared with evidence for asthma and allergic sensitization. Future studies should identify specific microbial, metabolic, and immune pathways that mediate protection and determine whether safe, defined surrogates of farm exposure can be translated into food allergy prevention strategies.
journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology

title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
abstract: NA: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

title: CXCL16-CXCR6 axis drives the enrichment of CCR8+ effector regulatory T cells and shapes an immunosuppressive microenvironment in the colorectal cancer liver metastatic niche.
abstract: NA: The mechanisms underlying regulatory T cell (Treg) enrichment and immunosuppressive activity in colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis with experimental and tissue-based validation to investigate Treg heterogeneity and its potential regulation in CRLM. Our findings revealed a shift toward effector Treg states in metastatic lesions, characterized by increased CCR8 expression and associated with an immunosuppressive landscape. CellChat analysis identified CXCL16-CXCR6 as a candidate signaling axis between myeloid or dendritic populations and effector Tregs. In vitro chemotaxis assays demonstrated preferential migration of CCR8+ Tregs toward CXCL16, and this response was attenuated by CXCR6 blockade. Analyses of human CRLM cohorts and tissue samples further linked CCR8+ effector Treg enrichment to reduced effector T-cell abundance and increased inhibitory-checkpoint expression. Collectively, these findings implicate CXCL16-CXCR6-mediated chemotaxis in the accumulation of effector Tregs with immunosuppressive features in CRLM and highlight CCR8 as a marker of these Treg states, providing insight into the interplay between CXCL16-expressing myeloid populations and Tregs in the metastatic liver microenvironment.

title: Mechanisms and Implications of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Hematopoietic System.
abstract: NA: COVID-19 disrupts hematopoiesis across the entire hierarchy, from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) to mature blood cells. Several hematological abnormalities-lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer-are consistently associated with disease severity and mortality. Within the HSPC compartment, ACE2 and TMPRSS2 expression is largely restricted to rare CD133 + CD34+Lin-CD45 - precursors, suggesting that hematopoietic injury may arise substantially from non-infectious exposure to spike protein and inflammatory mediators rather than from direct viral infection. Downstream events include NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, virus-induced senescence with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype, epigenetic reprogramming, and skewed lineage output. These cell-intrinsic changes are compounded by remodeling of the bone marrow niche by stromal, endothelial, and osteoblastic cells. Clinically, these changes manifest as lymphopenia with T-cell exhaustion and disturbed regulatory T-cell balance, thrombocytopenia due to impaired megakaryopoiesis and immune-mediated clearance, coagulopathy involving neutrophil extracellular trap formation and endothelial injury, and anemia reflecting disordered iron handling and red-cell damage. These abnormalities can persist in a subset of patients long after viral clearance. These mechanistic insights inform current management, including antiviral therapy for prolonged viral shedding, corticosteroids for severe disease, severity-stratified anticoagulation, and supportive measures to promote marrow recovery. The hematological implications of vaccination are also considered: although rare immune thrombotic events have been reported, their mechanism appears distinct from spike-protein-induced injury, and the overall benefit-risk balance of vaccination remains favorable. We distinguish conclusions supported by clinical data from those based on in vitro or observational evidence and highlight open questions for future research.

title: Immune cell mediated fibrosis after kidney transplantation: mechanisms and emerging immunomodulatory therapies.
abstract: NA: Renal allograft fibrosis is a common histological endpoint after multiple injuries, rather than an independent disease entity. Despite modern immunosuppression, recurrent alloimmune injury, ischemia reperfusion injury, infection, donor and recipient related factors, and drug toxicity can converge on interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. This review examines how innate and adaptive immune responses contribute to the transition from early graft injury to chronic remodeling, with particular emphasis on cellular plasticity and intercellular communication. Human single cell and spatial studies show that immune, tubular epithelial, endothelial, and stromal cells form heterogeneous, stage dependent networks rather than fixed pathogenic populations. We prioritize evidence from human kidney allografts while clearly identifying mechanisms inferred from experimental models. Established immunosuppression remains essential for preventing immune mediated graft injury, whereas regulatory T cell therapies, macrophage state modulation, cytokine blockade, and CD38 directed therapy remain investigational. None has been proven to reverse established allograft fibrosis. Future diagnosis and treatment should integrate Banff histology, donor specific antibodies, donor derived cell free DNA, urinary chemokines, and biopsy-based transcriptomics. Clinical trials should determine whether targeted immunomodulation can slow the progression of allograft fibrosis and preserve long-term graft function and survival.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

title: Peripheral Blood Transcriptomic Candidates Associated With Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome and Pseudoexfoliation Glaucoma: A Bioinformatics Analysis.
abstract: NA: The molecular mechanism of pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG) is still unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers of PXG, with the goal of providing a theoretical basis. Ten blood samples from patients with pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX), 10 blood samples from PXG patients, and 10 control blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. A total of three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, and MMP9) were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that the three candidate biomarkers were involved in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton and the leukocyte transendothelial migration pathway. The results of the peripheral immune cell proportion analysis suggested altered peripheral immune profiles among the three groups, involving memory B-cells, CD8+ T-cells, regulatory T-cells, M0 macrophages, and resting CD4+ memory T-cells. Correlation analysis further revealed associations between the candidate biomarkers and these differential immune cell subsets. Exploratory drug‒gene interaction analysis provided preliminary insights for future therapeutic investigations. In an RT-qPCR validation set consisting of 15 peripheral whole blood samples (5 PEX, 5 PXG, and 5 control samples), the mRNA expression levels of the candidate biomarkers were assessed across the three groups. RT-qPCR validation revealed that ACTA2 and MMP9 were significantly upregulated in PXG patients compared with controls, whereas ACTA2, MMP9, and IL1RN were elevated in PEX patients compared with both controls and PXG patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the three candidate biomarkers may be associated with PEX/PXG-related molecular alterations.

title: Oncolytic Viruses Armed with Multiple Immunomodulatory Transgenes in Cancer Immunotherapy.
abstract: NA: Oncolytic viruses (OVs) have emerged as versatile cancer immunotherapeutic agents that selectively kill tumor cells while simultaneously inducing antitumor immune responses. The therapeutic activity of OVs can be further enhanced by arming them with immunomodulatory transgenes. However, expression of a single transgene often fails to generate durable antitumor immunity, largely because of the complex, immunosuppressive nature of the tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome this limitation, recent advances in OV engineering have focused on co-expression of multiple immunomodulatory payloads, including a combination of cytokines, cytokine receptors, costimulatory molecules, chemokines, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), bispecific T-cell engagers, viral antigens, and tumor antigens. Increasing evidence indicates that multi-transgene-armed OVs can more effectively promote dendritic cell maturation, enhance intratumoral infiltration and activation of CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells, elevate effector-to-regulatory T-cell ratios, remodel immunosuppressive TMEs, and synergize with other immunotherapies, including ICI and adoptive cell therapy. Despite growing interest in this field, a comprehensive review focused specifically on the immunological mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and translational challenges of multi-transgene-expressing OVs remains lacking. In this review, we summarize multi-transgene-armed OVs, highlighting the mechanistic rationale underlying transgene combinations, outlining their antitumor effects across preclinical settings, and discussing key design principles for next-generation OV-based immunotherapies.

title: Thioredoxin-1 induces immune tolerance against α-syn presented by MHC-II in microglia via promoting Tregs differentiation in MPTP-induced Parkinson's disease mice.
abstract: NA: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disease characterized by the loss of dopaminergic (DAergic) neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and the formation of Lewy bodies composed of misfolded alpha-synuclein (α-syn). A growing number of studies indicate that microglia-mediated neuroinflammation and autoimmune responses are important pathological features of PD. Thioredoxin-1 (Trx-1), a multifunctional redox-regulatory protein, exerts neuroprotective effects in 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced PD models, but its impact on microglia-mediated autoimmune responses in PD remains unexplored. In the present study, we demonstrated that Trx-1 suppressed microglial accumulation and the increase of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Furthermore, Trx-1 suppressed the increase of α-syn and major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II)-mediated antigen presentation in microglia induced by MPTP. Additionally, MPTP promoted T helper 17 (Th17) cell differentiation, inhibited forkhead box P3 (FOXP3) protein level and regulatory T (Treg) cell differentiation, and enhanced forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) phosphorylation and nuclear exclusion in the SNpc. All these pathological alterations induced by MPTP were effectively restored by Trx-1 overexpression. Our findings highlight the pivotal role of Trx-1 in microglia-mediated autoimmune responses, thereby providing a potential therapeutic target for PD.

title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses characterize an IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern in extracellular matrix remodeling and Treg-associated immune suppression in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. As an important N6-methyladenosine (m6A) reader, insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its downstream regulatory network and potential role in immune microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: Public datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed to identify prognostic IGF2BP3-related genes. Functional enrichment analysis, prognostic model construction, immune infiltration analysis, somatic mutation profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic analysis, and CellChat-based cell-cell communication analysis were performed. In vitro experiments, including qRT-PCR, western blotting, wound healing, transwell, CCK-8, and RNA stability assays, were conducted to evaluate the cellular effects of IGF2BP3 silencing. Multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model, drug sensitivity analysis, and molecular docking were further performed to explore immune microenvironment associations and potential therapeutic implications.
RESULTS: IGF2BP3 was significantly upregulated in PAAD and associated with poor prognosis. MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 were identified as candidate IGF2BP3-associated ECM-related genes. IGF2BP3 knockdown was associated with changes in the proliferation, migration, and invasion of Panc-1 cells and was accompanied by decreased stability of these transcripts. A prognostic signature consisting of IGF2BP3, MMP1, MMP7, and ITGA2 demonstrated consistent prognostic stratification across multiple independent cohorts. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed predominant expression of these genes in epithelial cell populations and highlighted their potential association with PAAD-related cellular states and intercellular communication. Among the downstream targets, MMP7 emerged as a candidate downstream effector based on RNA stability assays, SHAP feature importance analysis, gene interaction network analysis, and single-cell expression profiling. Both IGF2BP3 and MMP7 were positively associated with regulatory T-cell (Treg) infiltration. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further demonstrated significant spatial correlations among IGF2BP3, MMP7, and Treg-enriched immune niches, while multiplex immunofluorescence, immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic syngeneic mouse model supported their association with immunosuppressive microenvironment features. Drug sensitivity analysis computationally prioritized Trametinib as a candidate for further investigation in high-risk PAAD, while molecular docking suggested favorable predicted interactions between Trametinib and the four signature proteins.
CONCLUSIONS: IGF2BP3 was associated with PAAD progression, and its depletion was accompanied by reduced stability of ECM-associated transcripts and changes in the tumor immune microenvironment. Integrated bulk transcriptomic, single-cell transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and experimental analyses identify MMP7 as a candidate downstream effector associated with IGF2BP3 and suggest that the IGF2BP3-MMP7-associated pattern is related to Treg-enriched immunosuppressive niches in PAAD. Furthermore, Trametinib was identified as a hypothesis-generating therapeutic candidate for further evaluation in high-risk PAAD.

title: Oral Bacillus subtilis attenuates house dust mite-induced atopic dermatitis and is associated with altered mucosal immune responses.
abstract: NA: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease often presenting in infancy and increases the risk of developing other atopic disorders including food allergy, allergic rhinitis, and asthma. The rising prevalence of allergic diseases correlates with increasingly sterile living environments and reduced exposure to bacteria. This study hypothesized that exposure to nonpathogenic bacteria could help educate the immune system toward tolerance to innocuous allergens. Oral delivery of the probiotic bacterium Bacillus subtilis was used in a murine model of house dust mite (HDM)-induced AD. Oral administration of B. subtilis significantly reduced clinical symptoms of HDM-induced AD at weeks 3 and 7. B. subtilis treatment also reduced mast cell numbers in the skin at week 7 and showed a trend toward reducing epidermal thickness at week 3, although this was not statistically significant and was lost by week 7. While B. subtilis did not significantly reduce HDM-specific or total IgE or IgG1 levels, it increased levels of total IgA. The study found no significant changes in regulatory T cell numbers in the skin-draining lymph nodes. However, Treg numbers in the small intestine statistically increased 1 week after B. subtilis treatment. These findings support the role of probiotic treatment with B. subtilis as a tool to reduce the development and clinical symptoms of AD, associated with reduced mast cell accumulation, increased IgA levels, and increased intestinal regulatory T cell frequencies.

title: Aging drives distinct chromatin signatures of CD8 T cell dysfunction and the emergence of a unique CD8 Treg cell population.
abstract: NA: Aging profoundly alters CD8 T cells, driving senescence and exhaustion that contribute to immune decline. By mapping chromatin accessibility across functional and dysfunctional CD8 T cell subsets from young and aged mice, we found that age-related CD8 T cell dysfunction was associated with a loss of regulation at three distinct levels. Dysfunctional CD8 T cells showed reduced accessibility of genes essential for "stemness," indicating diminished regenerative potential. Exhausted memory T cells (Tmem cells) showed decreased accessibility of "restraint" genes, which limit differentiation postactivation. Last, both senescent virtual memory T cells (TVM cells) and exhausted Tmem cells displayed increased accessibility of "terminal inhibitory" genes, underscoring progression toward irreversible dysfunction. The inhibitory receptor gene Fcgr2b, encoding FcγRIIb/CD32b, was notably increased in a subset of aged TVM cells with regulatory characteristics. This study defines mechanisms of CD8 T cell aging and identifies a CD8 regulatory T cell (Treg cell) population that emerges as a hallmark of aging.

title: Causal associations between immune cell traits and hip osteoarthritis: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
abstract: NA: Observational studies have reported associations between immune cell phenotypes and hip osteoarthritis (HOA), but whether these associations are causal is unknown. We, therefore, used bidirectional 2-sample mendelian randomization (MR) to examine potential causal associations between 731 immune cell traits and HOA risk. Genome-Wide Association Study summary data for 731 immune cell traits were obtained from the genome-wide association study catalog, and HOA summary data were derived from the FinnGen Consortium. Instrumental variables were selected using significance thresholds of P < 1 × 10-5 for immune traits and P < 5 × 10-8 for HOA. The primary analysis used inverse variance weighted (IVW) MR, complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode methods. Sensitivity analyses included Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, mendelian randomization pleiotropy residual sum and outlier test, and leave-one-out analysis. False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple testing. In the forward MR analysis, IVW identified 17 immune traits with FDR-significant associations with HOA risk (FDR < 0.05). Six CD33-expressing myeloid cell traits showed positive associations with HOA risk (odds ratio = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03 for all), while eleven immune traits including T cell, B cell, Natural Killer cell, regulatory T cell , and conventional dendritic cell phenotypes showed inverse associations (odds ratio range: 0.90-0.97), suggesting a potential protective role. Sensitivity analyses did not detect significant heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy for any of these 17 associations (all MR-Egger intercept P > .05; all Cochran's Q P > .05). Weighted median estimates were directionally concordant with IVW for all 17 traits, and every association met the prespecified cross-method consistency criterion (at least three of 5 methods directionally concordant). In the reverse MR analysis, 19 immune traits showed nominal associations (P < .05); however, none survived FDR correction (FDR > 0.05), providing no robust evidence for causal effects of HOA on immune cell composition. This MR study provides genetic evidence linking CD33-related myeloid traits and multiple lymphoid and monocyte phenotypes to HOA risk. These associations are statistical and do not establish biological mechanisms. Future experimental and clinical studies are needed to determine whether these immune phenotypes contribute to HOA pathophysiology.

title: Immunomodulatory effect of neem leaf glycoprotein (NLGP) through TH1 polarisation and regulatory Treg-associated gene modulation in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
abstract: NA: Neem leaf glycoprotein (NLGP), derived from Azadirachta indica, is an immune activator with potential in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) immunotherapy. NSCLC progression supported by regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) activity and blunt TH1-type responses. We tested whether NLGP can reduce Treg-mediated immunosuppression and shift adaptive immunity towards a tumoricidal TH1-profile. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy controls and NSCLC patients were treated with NLGP and assessed by MTT [3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide], Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), nitric oxide (NO) assays, and qRT-PCR. NLGP treatment produced maximal lymphocyte proliferation, increased CTL-mediated cytotoxicity, and elevated NO release-an effector molecule known to favour TH1 responses. Cytokine profiling showed increased type1-cytokines and upregulation of TH1-specific genes, while TH2-, TH17-, and Treg-associated gene expression declined. Notably, IL10 and Forkhead box P3 (FOXP3) expression dropped after NLGP treatment, indicating suppressed Treg function. These results suggest NLGP promotes antitumor immunity in NSCLC by enhancing CTL activity and TH1 polarisation while restraining Treg-mediated suppression.

title: Immune microenvironment in radiation-induced intestinal injury: role, mechanism and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: NA: Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) represents the primary dose-limiting toxicity of abdominopelvic radiotherapy. Its progression to chronic lesions marked by fibrosis and vascular sclerosis stems not merely from direct epithelial damage, but predominantly from dynamic remodeling of the intestinal immune microenvironment. This review systematically dissects stage-dependent immune cascades underlying RIII: damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) from damaged epithelia trigger innate immune activation through TLR4/NLRP3/cGAS-STING axes; neutrophils and M1 macrophages fuel a self-perpetuating TNF-necroptosis-DAMP inflammatory loop; dendritic cell-mediated Th1/Th17 polarization may contribute to the transition to chronic injury; balanced macrophage repolarization, regulatory T cell (Treg) expansion, IL-22-dependent epithelial repair and commensal metabolites jointly determine inflammation resolution. Critically, we highlight three translational constraints: (i) limited extrapolability of single high-dose mouse data to clinical fractionated radiotherapy, (ii) phase-dependent opposing effects of therapeutic targets and (iii) shared core immune pathways creating a fundamental trade-off between intestinal radioprotection and radiotherapy-induced antitumor immunity. Accordingly, we advocate shifting the research focus in RIII from target screening to validating risk-stratified biomarkers, building tumor-bearing fractionated animal models with dual efficacy endpoints and developing spatial/temporal/target-selective decoupling regimens to separate normal gut protection from suppression of antitumor immunity.

title: Stem Cells and Derivatives in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Mechanisms, Sources, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: NA: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, are chronic, relapsing disorders of the gastrointestinal tract for which a substantial proportion of patients fail to respond to current therapies, underscoring the need for novel strategies. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and their derivatives have emerged as a promising frontier in regenerative medicine, owing to their self-renewal capacity, multilineage differentiation, and potent immunomodulatory properties. MSCs modulate the intestinal microenvironment by suppressing effector T-cell responses, expanding regulatory T (Treg) and B (Breg) cells, polarizing macrophages toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes, reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines, and shaping the gut microbiota. Most of these effects are mediated by paracrine signals carried by the MSC secretome and extracellular vesicles (EVs), which deliver cytokines, microRNAs, and proteins that promote tissue repair, angiogenesis, and resolution of inflammation. Cell-free approaches based on conditioned medium or exosomes offer further advantages over direct cell transplantation, including improved safety, easier standardization, and reduced immunogenicity. MSCs derived from bone marrow, adipose tissue, and perinatal tissues each show distinct biological and therapeutic features. The treatment of complex perianal fistulas in Crohn's disease is the most clinically advanced application, with darvadstrocel demonstrating safety and efficacy in clinical trials. Additional emerging indications include intestinal fibrosis and tissue regeneration. Key challenges remain, including cellular heterogeneity, lack of standardized manufacturing, and optimization of dosing and delivery. Future perspectives point toward a paradigm shift from cell-based therapies to next generation cell-free strategies, including secretome-derived formulations and engineered extracellular vescicles, which may provide safer, more scalable and ultimately disease-modifying therapeutic options for patients with IBD.

title: Resolvin D1 Treatment Ameliorates Autoimmune Thyroiditis and Modulates the T Helper 17/Regulatory T-Cell Balance in NOD.H-2h4 Mice.
abstract: NA: Autoimmune thyroiditis (AIT) is a prevalent autoimmune disease associated with an imbalance between T helper 17 (Th17) and regulatory T (Treg) cells, yet effective disease-modifying therapies are lacking. We hypothesized that the pro-resolving mediator Resolvin D1 (RvD1) could ameliorate AIT by restoring this immune balance. Forty female NOD.H-2h4 mice were allocated to four groups (n = 10/group). Mice in the AIT groups received drinking water containing 0.05% sodium iodide (NaI) for 8 weeks to induce AIT; NaI was withdrawn at the end of week 8. During weeks 9-12, mice received RvD1 at 100 ng/mouse (approximately 5 μg/kg) or 300 ng/mouse (approximately 15 μg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection three times weekly. Serum thyroid indices, tissue cytokines, and splenic Th17/Treg measures were analyzed in three mice per group, and histopathological scoring was analyzed in nine mice per group. RvD1 treatment reduced several AIT measures. The low dose produced a numerical decrease in thyroglobulin antibody levels without statistical significance, whereas the high dose significantly decreased these levels. RvD1 improved thyroid indices and decreased histological inflammation and pro-inflammatory cytokines. RvD1 also decreased splenic Th17 proportions, increased Treg proportions, and lowered the Th17/Treg ratio. RvD1 ameliorated several manifestations of AIT and was associated with restoration of the splenic Th17/Treg balance, supporting further investigation of RvD1 as an immunomodulatory approach in AIT.

title: Immunoglobulin G4-Related Pericarditis With Forkhead Box P3-Positive Cells in Lymphoid Follicles Identified by Pericardial Biopsy: A Case Report.
abstract: NA: T-follicular regulatory (Tfr) cells have been implicated in immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD). A 62-year-old woman presented with dyspnea caused by recurrent right pleural effusion. Serum IgG4 level was elevated to 194 mg/dL, and computed tomography revealed right pericardial thickening. Because pleural fluid studies were nondiagnostic and no macroscopic pleural abnormalities were found during surgery, an abnormal pericardium was biopsied. Histology showed lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with an IgG4/IgG ratio > 85% and 63.3 IgG4-positive plasma cells/high-power field. Numerous forkhead box P3 (FOXP3)-positive cells were present within the lymphoid follicles, suggesting the involvement of regulatory T-cell/Tfr-related immune responses. The patient was diagnosed with IgG4-related pericarditis and treated with prednisolone 0.6 mg/kg, resulting in marked reduction of pleural effusion. FOXP3-positive cells may provide adjunctive immunopathological information, and biopsy of an abnormal pericardium may aid in diagnosis when pleural and pericardial lesions coexist.

title: Mechanobiology of regulatory T cells: how cellular mechanics shape immune suppression.
abstract: NA: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) suppress immune responses through multiple mechanisms, including contact-dependent removal of pMHCII and costimulatory ligands from antigen-presenting cells via trogocytosis and trans-endocytosis. These pathways require membrane deformation, receptor engagement, and vesicular trafficking. We propose that Treg efficiency in these processes is shaped by cellular mechanics-particularly membrane tension and actin organization-yielding a distinct biophysical signature for antigen-specific suppression.

title: Extracellular vesicles in osteoporosis and osteoimmunity: a systematic evidence map.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis extracellular vesicle (EV) research includes many proposed cargoes and therapeutic constructs, but molecular perturbation, vesicle-specific attribution, and evidence in humans answer different questions.
OBJECTIVE: We asked 1) where osteoporosis EV studies are concentrated across osteoimmune mechanisms and study stages, 2) how often advanced mechanistic perturbation occurs together with human evidence, and 3) which experiment is missing when a mechanistic, biomarker, or therapeutic claim remains unsupported.
METHODS: Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus supplied the historical set; PubMed and Embase used equivalent osteoporosis/bone-loss and EV/exosome concepts through 16 April 2026. Full-text primary studies were classified by osteoimmune directness, mechanistic-perturbation depth, human linkage, and seven overlapping modules. Risk of bias, reporting completeness, and MISEV2023 reporting were assessed separately.
RESULTS: The corrected map contained 222 primary studies: 36 (16.2%) were human-linked, 201 (90.5%) contained animal work, and 213 (95.9%) contained in vitro work. Advanced mechanistic perturbation occurred in 115 studies (51.8%); 13 studies combined this category with human linkage, 102 were advanced without human evidence, 23 were human-linked without advanced perturbation, and 84 had neither. The remodeling interface was the largest module (n = 120), followed by non-classical particles (n = 44), engineered delivery (n = 43), macrophage/monocyte biology (n = 35), and ageing/senescence (n = 28). Eight studies entered the T-cell/Treg/Th17 module. One engineered-delivery study linked an osteoblast intervention to B lymphopoiesis; no eligible study establishing an endogenous B cell-derived EV route was identified.
CONCLUSION: Candidate cargoes are abundant, but few studies connect a defined donor state and active vesicular fraction to an osteoimmune mediator, a skeletal outcome, and an intended human claim. The map identifies the untested link and the study design needed to evaluate it while keeping separate evidence dimensions distinct.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://osf.io/zdcj2/, identifier zdcj2.

title: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity.
abstract: NA: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

title: MHCII + cancer-associated fibroblasts promote antitumor immunity in pancreatic cancer.
abstract: NA: The functions of major histocompatibility complex class II molecule-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (MHCII + CAFs) in pancreatic cancer remain controversial. MHCII + CAFs are primarily described as immunosuppressive, as MHCII allows for direct interaction with, and support of, regulatory T cells (Tregs). However, MHCII + CAF functions may be more complex depending on their origins and their cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Here, using orthotopic models of pancreatic cancer, we show that conventional CD4 + T cells and their production of Interferon gamma (IFNγ) increased MHCII + CAFs in tumors. Acute depletion of Tregs using Foxp3 DTR mice revealed that Tregs suppress the abundance of MHCII + CAFs in tumors by inhibiting CD4 T cell responses that can directly control primary tumor growth and metastatic progression. Functionally, MHCII expression on fibroblasts was required for CD4 T cell control of PDAC progression upon Treg ablation. Collectively, our findings identify an IFNγ-driven, antitumor activity of MHCII expression on CAFs and reveal that CAFs may be harnessed to promote adaptive immunity to PDAC.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Deep phenomics of human PBMCs using a 31-marker spectral flow cytometry panel.
abstract: NA: Functional cytokines orchestrate leukocyte-mediated innate and adaptive immune responses within the host following infection or immunization. In contrast, lymphocyte-mediated activation-induced markers (AIMs) are predominantly associated with adaptive immune responses. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) primarily function to balance the immune response by preventing excessive inflammation and maintaining self-tolerance. Currently, conventional intracellular cytokine tracking or cytokine-independent AIMs methodology is available for studying antigen-specific lymphocyte or T cell responses in humans. However, this approach faces challenges due to the difficulty in simultaneously deep immunophenotyping the key functional cytokine signatures, AIMs, and nuclear signature of FoxP3 + Tregs. Using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 31-parameter panel to profile simultaneously major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) along with T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFNγ, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, AIMs and FoxP3 + Tregs in human PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated. We also re-validated our panel to profile antigen specific Th1/2/17 cells or AIMs distribution after peptide stimulation. This optimized multicolor spectral flow panel allows a detailed immune profiling of functional cytokines, AIMs and FoxP3 + Tregs in the T cell compartment from human and might be useful for exploratory analysis of how these functional cytokines or AIMs or Tregs shape host immunity after infection or vaccination. Our panel is highly customizable, allowing researchers to tailor it to their specific requirements.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Clonally Convergent Tph/Tfh-like CD4 + T Cells are Shared Across Recovery and Recurrence in Experimental Periodontitis.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the tooth-supporting structures (periodontium) that requires life-long maintenance to prevent progression. Using a sensitized model of recurrent periodontitis in mice (SeRPD), in which regulatory breakdown was induced by temporary Treg depletion concurrent with disease, we mapped the gingival T cell imprint across each disease phase. Transient regulatory breakdown left a durable mucosal imprint after clinical recovery, characterized by enrichment of local and regional CD4⁺ T cells. Paired single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing of gingival immune cells identified a convergent clonotype expanded from recovery into recurrence that carried a Tfh/Tph-like transcriptional identity. An analogous CD4⁺ T cell population was detected in human periodontitis lesions by single-cell transcriptomics. Together, these findings support a paradigm in which clinical recovery does not ensure a local T cell repertoire reset; instead, a reservoir of antigen-experienced, tissue-adapted CD4⁺ T cells persist in the mucosa and participate in recurrence.
HIGHLIGHTS: The murine SeRPD model induced local and regional enrichment of antigen-experienced CD4 + T cells. A clonally expanded convergent clonotype was shared in recovery and recurrence phases. After clinical recovery, convergent CD4 + T clones expressed a Tfh/Tph-like program. Human periodontitis lesions were associated with an analogous Tfh/Tph-like population.
IN BRIEF: Sharma et al. show that periodontitis accompanied by regulatory breakdown, leaves a lasting, clonally expanded Tfh/Tph-like population within recovered gingiva that is also present during recurrence. A comparable CD4 + T cell-population was associated with human periodontitis, suggesting a memory reservoir for relapse.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: CCR8⁺ regulatory T cell depletion overcomes immune checkpoint blockade resistance in BRCA2-deficient prostate cancer.
abstract: NA: BRCA2 -mutated prostate cancer is an aggressive, genomically unstable subtype, yet how this genomic instability influences tumor immunity remains undefined. We developed an isogenic, immunocompetent model of Brca2 -deficient prostate cancer in which BRCA2 loss activated the cGAS/STING pathway and a type I interferon response across multiple cellular compartments, paradoxically leading to an overall immunosuppressed tumor microenvironment. Within this microenvironment, tumor-associated macrophages were interferon-responsive and expressed the CCR8 ligand Ccl8 , and there was enrichment of immunosuppressive CCR8⁺ regulatory T cells (Treg). Anti-PD-1 monotherapy was ineffective and instead reinforced this immunosuppressive circuit, leading to expansion of CCR8⁺ Tregs. However, depletion of CCR8⁺ regulatory T cells overcame resistance to checkpoint blockade. Analysis of human BRCA2 -mutated prostate cancer showed elevated CCR8 expression, supporting the translational relevance of the CCR8⁺ Treg axis as a potential therapeutic target in a disease largely refractory to immunotherapy.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Deep phenomics of African green monkey and Baboon PBMCs using a 30-marker spectral flow cytometry panel.
abstract: NA: Vaccines are the best way to prevent and combat diseases. Non-human primate (NHP) models have proven to be the gold standard model for studying the efficacy of certain vaccine candidates prior to human trials. Cell-mediated immunity serves as a surrogate marker for predicting vaccine efficacy. Despite the availability of deep-immunophenotyping panels for T cells in the peripheral blood of humans, their application to NHPs, particularly African Green Monkeys (AGMs) and baboons, remains limited. Notably, AGMs are valuable for HIV and COVID-19 research, while baboons are utilized for pertussis research as a natural infection model and vaccine trial. To overcome such limitation, using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 30-parameter panel to profile major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) either in AGM or baboon PBMCs. We also profiled T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFNγ, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, activation-induced markers (AIMs) and FoxP3 + Tregs in both AGM and baboon PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated in both NHP species. This panel holds potential for exploratory analysis of the impact of these functional cytokines, AIMs, or Tregs on host immunity following infection or vaccination. The panel's high level of customization empowers researchers to tailor it to their specific research needs.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Epigenetic Mechanisms Inhibit Smad7 and Contribute to Fibrosis in Crohn's Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: TGF-β1 is a central regulator of profibrotic gene expression, extracellular matrix deposition, and the development of intestinal fibrosis in patients with fibrostenotic Crohn's disease (CD). Unlike the increased expression of Smad7 in mucosal and lamina propria monocytes, where it impairs Treg function, mesenchymal cells from patients with fibrostenotic CD do not exhibit elevated Smad7 expression and instead display sustained TGF-β1 signaling. We therefore sought to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the unexpected silencing of Smad7 in fibrostenotic CD.
METHODS: Subepithelial myofibroblasts (SEMFs) and muscularis smooth muscle cells were isolated from paired normal and affected ileal tissues obtained from the same patients with each Montreal phenotype of CD, as well as from non-CD controls. Gene expression, RNA-binding affinity, transcriptional activity, promoter methylation, protein levels, and the mechanisms that regulate Smad7 expression were evaluated in ex vivo tissues and primary cultured cells. MicroRNA-21 (miR-21) localization was assessed by RNAscope. miR-21-mediated suppression of Smad7 was investigated using antagomiR-21. Smad7 silencing through promoter hypermethylation was confirmed using 5-Azacytidine treatment and DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) knockdown. Smad7 lysine acetylation and Smurf1/2-mediated ubiquitination were examined using selective inhibitors and proximity ligation assays.
RESULTS: In SEMFs from patients with fibrostenotic CD, aberrant silencing of Smad7 resulted from DNMT1-dependent promoter hypermethylation and pSmad3-driven, miR-21-mediated degradation of Smad7 mRNA. In addition, Smurf1/2 promoted ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of acetylated Smad7 protein. Inhibition of miR-21 with antagomiR-21 restored Smad7 expression and reduced TGF-β1-dependent profibrotic gene expression. Likewise, demethylation with 5-Azacytidine or knockdown of DNMT1 induced Smad7 promoter hypomethylation and restored Smad7 expression. Furthermore, modulation of the balance between p300 acetyltransferase and histone deacetylase 1 (HDAC1) stabilized Smad7 protein by protecting it from degradation.
CONCLUSIONS: A distinctive pattern of epigenetic silencing and post-translational regulation of Smad7 was identified in patients with fibrostenotic CD. These mechanisms collectively promote unrestrained TGF-β1 signaling by suppressing Smad7 expression and stability in SEMFs, thereby contributing to the development of intestinal fibrosis.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: T cell receptors from CD8 regulatory T cells direct the development of natural intraepithelial lymphocytes.
abstract: NA: CD8 regulatory T cells (CD8 Tregs) in mice have been identified by their expression of the surface receptor family Ly49 and the transcription factor Helios. To our surprise, many Ly49+ and Helios+ T cells express neither CD4 nor CD8, and many express only CD8αα. We found that CD8 Tregs in the spleen are linked to the CD8β- natural intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) that reside in the small intestine. Blocking trafficking to the intestine increased splenic CD8 Treg frequency, and transferred splenic CD8 Tregs gave rise to natural IELs. Unexpectedly, Helios was dispensable for natural IEL development, arguing against its role as a shared lineage-determining transcription factor. Instead, we found that T cell receptors (TCRs) from splenic Ly49+ CD8 Tregs deterministically direct natural IEL development. Our findings suggest that CD8 Tregs may derive from the same TCR-directed developmental program that generates natural IELs and shed light on the origins of these immunoregulatory cells.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Cytotoxic CD4+ exTregs expressing KLRG1 retain immunosuppressive function in cancer.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: The role of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells in cancer remains controversial, with both pro- and anti-tumor functionality described. Based on a prior observation that putatively cytotoxic KLRG1+ FoxP3-conventional T cells (Tconv) associated with tumor progression, we deeply investigated the phenotype and function of KLRG1+ Tconv in multiple murine tumor models and in human clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) specimens. We found KLRG1+ Tconv have a conserved, highly activated, terminally differentiated phenotype across species. In murine tumors, KLRG1+ Tconv resemble tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs) at both transcriptional and proteomic levels, upregulating a spectrum of exhaustion-related checkpoint receptors, producing IL-10 and granzyme B (GzmB), and silencing expression of IFNγ and TNFα. Functionally, KLRG1+ Tconv exhibited immunosuppressive function in ex vivo assays. Using an in vivo Treg fate mapping approach in tumor-bearing mice, we found a subset of KLRG1+ Tconv are derived from Tregs that have lost FoxP3 protein expression. Ex vivo functional assays demonstrated the exTreg component of the KLRG1+ Tconv compartment is responsible for IL-10 production and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In treatment studies, we found that KLRG1-targeted antibody-mediated depletion was more efficient than anti-KLRG1 blockade at slowing tumor growth and improving survival, with responses associating with depletion of intratumoral KLRG1+ Tconv and Tregs. In sum, our study discovered a novel conserved pathway of CD4+ T cell plasticity, wherein intratumoral, cytotoxic KLRG1+ CD4+ Tconv cells can be derived from Tregs and maintain immunosuppressive function, despite loss of FoxP3, and that KLRG1-targeted depletion may outperform KLRG1 blockade as an immunotherapeutic strategy in cancer.
ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY: KLRG1-expressing FoxP3-negative CD4+ T cells in tumors harbor a pool of exTregs that retain an immunosuppressive and cytotoxic profile.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Single-cell Profiling of Airway-associated CD4+ T cells in Metal-induced Hypersensitivity.
abstract: NA: Omics-based approaches are increasingly used to identify unique molecular signatures that may serve as biomarkers for early disease detection and potential therapeutic targets. Chronic beryllium disease (CBD), resulting from beryllium-induced hypersensitivity, is characterized by the accumulation and expansion of pathogenic CD4+ T cells in the lungs, ultimately contributing to impaired pulmonary function. In this study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on sorted viable bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cells from beryllium-exposed patients (n=2) and compared their transcriptional profiles with publicly available scRNA-seq datasets from healthy controls (n=10). We identified 11 distinct CD3-associated cell clusters comprising T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, and regulatory T cells. Further analysis of CD4+ T cells from beryllium-exposed patients revealed increased expression of genes associated with T cell activation, immune regulation, and persistence, including IFNG, TNF, TNFAIP3, and CD74. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis further revealed upregulation of pathways associated with cellular activation, immune responses, and immune effector functions, whereas pathways related to metabolic processes were downregulated in beryllium samples compared with healthy controls. Overall, our findings identify distinct transcriptional signatures, including IFI27 and FABP4, in CD4+ T cells from beryllium-exposed patients, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying beryllium-induced pulmonary inflammation and highlighting potential candidates for further investigation as disease biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

title: Glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma (Review).
abstract: NA: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming, with glutamine addiction emerging as a central hallmark that extends beyond supporting tumor proliferation. This review synthesizes current knowledge on how glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma. The molecular basis of glutamine addiction is discussed, focusing on the von Hippel‑Lindau/hypoxia‑inducible factor axis, MYC activation and epigenetic regulation. The mechanisms by which glutamine metabolism orchestrates immune evasion are examined, including tumor immune cell competition, impaired effector T‑cell function, expansion of immunosuppressive populations such as regulatory T cells and M2 polarized macrophages, and upregulation of immune checkpoints. Therapeutic strategies targeting glutamine metabolism, from transporter and glutaminase inhibition to dietary restriction, are summarized along with mixed clinical trial outcomes that underscore the need for patient selection. Candidate predictive biomarkers across genetic, metabolic, immune and imaging domains are also reviewed. This review aims to provide an integrated framework for understanding glutamine‑driven immune modulation and to guide future therapeutic development in ccRCC.

title: Ascites-derived interleukin-10 drives tumor invasion in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer via STAT3 and ERK1/2 signaling.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a key immunoregulatory cytokine in ovarian cancer; however, its functional role and underlying mechanisms within the ascitic tumor microenvironment remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: We collected malignant ascites from 21 patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). IL-10 concentrations were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The association between ascitic IL-10 levels and clinicopathological parameters was analyzed. The effects of ascites-derived IL-10 on OC cell migration and invasion were evaluated in vitro, while in vivo experiments were conducted to assess the therapeutic potential of IL-10 neutralization. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) and M2 macrophages in ascites were characterized by flow cytometry and immunomagnetic bead sorting.
RESULTS: IL-10 levels in malignant ascites varied markedly among patients (134.38±84.80 pg/mL) and were positively correlated with serum cancer antigen 125 levels (r=0.553, p=0.014), while no statistically significant association was observed between ascitic IL-10 levels and ascites volume (r=0.312, p=0.207). Ascites-derived IL-10 significantly promoted EOC cell migration and invasion through activation of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 and extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 signaling pathways. In addition, Tregs (3.95±2.07%) and M2 macrophages (12.57±7.78%) were enriched in malignant ascites and served as important sources of IL-10, further enhancing the pro-invasive phenotype of EOC cells. Notably, IL-10 neutralization attenuated tumor progression in vivo.
CONCLUSION: These findings identify IL-10 as a biologically relevant immunosuppressive mediator within the EOC ascitic microenvironment that contributes to tumor invasiveness through immune cell-tumor cell crosstalk. Targeting ascites-derived IL-10 may represent a potential microenvironment-modulating strategy for controlling malignant ascites and invasive behavior in advanced EOC.

title: NGF-TRKA Facilitates the Activation of Lung Fibroblasts and Modulates the Immune Response in Pulmonary Fibrosis Via the FAK/ERK Signaling Pathway.
abstract: NA: A growing body of evidence suggests that immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF); however, the precise regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. We aim to identify key inflammatory factors and immune cells that significantly contribute to the onset and progression of IPF, and to elucidate their specific mechanisms of action. The potential causal relationships between 731 immunocyte phenotype, 41 inflammatory cytokines and IPF were conducted using bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (TwoSampleMR) analysis. The candidate targets were further screened in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF, as well as in both in vivo and in vitro models of pulmonary fibrosis (PF). In vitro experiments were performed by treating MRC5 cells with nerve growth factor (NGF) and the tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TRKA) inhibitor K-252a, or by transfecting the cells with siRNA targeting TRKA. Fibroblast activation was assessed using CCK-8 assays, wound healing assays, transwell migration assays, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), and western blot analysis. Additionally, co-immunoprecipitation (CoIP) was employed to verify the interaction between NGF and TRKA in MRC5 cells. In vivo studies examined the impact of NGF on immune responses and PF, as well as the antifibrotic effects of K-252a on these parameters. These evaluations were performed through histopathological examination, immunohistochemical analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, western blotting, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The genetically predicted onset of IPF has been correlated with the expression of NGF, which is significantly upregulated in the peripheral blood of individuals diagnosed with IPF. Furthermore, genetic analyses have implicated the involvement of two distinct immune cell populations in the initiation of IPF, with a particularly strong association observed between CD4 on CD39+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) and the risk of developing IPF (odds ratio [OR] = 1.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.00 - 1.28, false discovery rate-adjusted p-value [PFDR] = 0.0476). The cellular markers CD4, CD39 and Forkhead box P3 (FOXP3) exhibit elevated expression in murine models of PF. A positive correlation between NGF and the expression levels of CD4 and FOXP3 was also identified in patients with IPF. Mechanistically, NGF binds to its receptor TRKA, thereby activating the focal adhesion kinase / extracellular signal-regulated kinase (FAK / ERK) signaling pathway, which induces endoplasmic reticulum stress (ER stress) in pulmonary fibroblasts and promotes their activation. Additionally, NGF exacerbates bleomycin (BLM)-induced PF and enhances the expression of cellular markers characteristic of CD4+Foxp3+CD39+ activated Tregs, including CD4, CD39, FOXP3, interleukin-10 (IL-10), granzyme B (GZMB), and interleukin-2 receptor alpha (IL-2RA). Conversely, treatment with K-252a significantly inhibits the progression of PF and attenuates associated immunological responses.In murine models of pulmonary fibrosis, there is an increased co-localization of NGF with CD4, CD39, and FOXP3, whereas treatment with K-252a reduces this co-localization. Our findings indicate that the NGF-TRKA signaling pathway contributes to fibroblast activation and the cellular immune response in IPF. Consequently, targeting NGF-TRKA may constitute a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Only CD8+ T cell-derived IFN-γ is required to drive PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interferon gamma (IFN-γ) is a pleiotropic cytokine with a central yet complex role in anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. However, the key cellular sources of IFN-γ that are required for therapeutic efficacy remain undefined.
METHODS: We generated novel genetic models enabling cell type-specific Ifng deletion to selectively ablate IFN-γ production in CD8+ T cells, CD4+ conventional T cells (Tconvs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), or natural killer (NK) cells. MC38 and YUMMER1.7 tumor growth, survival, and responder ratios were assessed following anti-PD-1 or IgG control treatment. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were immunophenotyped by flow cytometry for evaluation of effector T-cell, exhaustion and activation markers. Two-way analysis of variance with mixed-effects modeling was used to compare tumor growth curves, and log-rank (Mantel-Cox) tests were performed for survival analysis. For flow cytometry analysis, statistical comparisons used two-tailed Mann-Whitney tests (multiple comparisons, 5% false discovery rate). Fisher’s exact tests were used for responder-class distributions.
RESULTS: We demonstrated that IFN-γ derived specifically from CD8+ T cells was required to drive anti-PD-1-mediated tumor control. This effect was not observed on deletion of Ifng in CD4+ Tconvs, Tregs, or NK cells.
